News.title: Young people aren't snowflakes - mental distress is rising, says head of official review
News.content:
Accusations that the young are a snowflake generation are wrong, the head of an independent review into mental health, ADHD and autism has told the BBC.

Prof Peter Fonagy said in an exclusive interview that there had been a real rise in mental distress among children and young people, with anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders the most common.

He said it was "harder to be young" now given the economic and employment uncertainty young people face, coupled with the challenges presented by social media.

His review was ordered nine months ago by Wes Streeting after the then-health secretary claimed in an interview that young people were over-diagnosed and "written off".

It is likely to feed into government policies on everything from NHS services and benefits to support for young people who are not in education, employment or training.

Fonagy said he chose to speak to the BBC ahead of the publication, which is expected later this week, because he was concerned the debate around ADHD and autism would "obscure" the wider issue of mental health.

Some have argued greater awareness and misattributing normal life stresses to mental illness were factors in the increase in cases.

Fonagy said his personal battle with mental health when he was young was a driving factor in his desire to help young people.

He experienced suicidal thoughts as a teenager after moving to London from Hungary without his parents. But he says he was fortunate to get therapy from a local service that "saved his life".

"It's harder to be young now," the 74-year-old said, adding that his review "dismisses the idea of a snowflake generation".

"I'm in awe of the way they have adjusted to an environment that is far more difficult than I ever had to face."

He said economic and employment uncertainty, as well as the pressures of social media, had created a "very toxic" environment for young people.

"They are a generation that has real serious challenges that I would not wish to have had when I was their age.

"Adults have let them down. We're the first generation that probably collectively feels we had a better life than our children will have.

"So, to the person who says it's a snowflake generation, just try living 24 hours as a 16-year-old."

News.title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out across England and Wales
News.content:
Labour promised in its 2024 manifesto to halve violence against women and girls within a decade.

"For too long, victims of rape and serious sexual offences have felt let down by our justice system," Burnham said.

"Prosecution rates for rape remain shamefully low, with many victims waiting years for justice. This is not good enough."

The changes were "long overdue" and would make a "significant difference" but focusing on prosecution alone would not be enough, he added.

"So as well as ensuring victims get justice, we will step up action to prevent these horrific crimes from happening in the first place," the prime minister said.

Nichols spoke publicly for the first time about being raped when she accused the then Justice Secretary, David Lammy, of using crime victims as a "cudgel" to push through his reforms of the legal system.

She was criticising the Courts and Tribunals Bill's plans to limit jury trials to cases with a likely prison sentence of three years or more.

She said she had waited 1,088 days to go to court, with every day being "agony" and the "trauma" made worse by her role in public life.

Her attacker, she said, was acquitted at crown court but subsequently ordered to pay compensation after she won a civil case against him.

"It is because I have been raped that I am as passionate as I am about what it means for a justice system to be truly victim-focused," she said.

"It is because I have endured every indignity that our broken criminal justice system could mete out that I care what kind of reform will actually deliver justice for survivors and victims of crime more widely."

Responding to news of the specialist courts being rolled out, the Conservatives said tackling delays to criminal rape trials was "long overdue" and they pushed Labour to commit to scrapping plans to restrict jury trials.

"The fact that victims have been withdrawing their cases because they have taken too long has been a disgrace," said shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy.

"Labour need to get courts sitting throughout the year, end the delays and clear the backlog â not undermine our right to a trial by jury."

Last year another charity, the Salford Survivor Project, said victims of rape and sexual assault were being "failed by the system" as court backlogs reached a record high.

The long delays for cases to go to trial were having a serious impact on victims' mental health, it said.

Also last year, a woman who says she was sexually assaulted by a taxi driver on her 21st birthday told BBC News she had dropped the case because of court delays.

She reported the alleged incident in early 2022 and gave evidence in court in December 2023 but the case was adjourned until September 2024 when the judge fell ill.

"I made the decision, even though I hate the statement, to drop the case," she said. "I couldn't let this hurt me further."

The Crown Prosecution Service said that, without her testimony, the case had been dropped because of insufficient evidence.

News.title: Oxford grooming gang survivors tell BBC 'hundreds' of abusers still free
News.content:
Warning: This story contains details of sexual violence

Survivors of an Oxford grooming gang say they still see men who sexually abused them, and who have not been brought to justice, walking around the city.

"A shop, a petrol station, a restaurant - everywhere you can imagine - you'll see a man that's done something," one survivor, Sarah, tells BBC Panorama.

Sarah and two other survivors believe "hundreds" of perpetrators are still free. An ex-police detective who led the initial investigation into grooming gangs in Oxford agrees.

It is the first time that Sarah (whose name we have changed) and one of the other women have spoken out publicly about what they were subjected to.

Gangs of men were found to have sexually exploited and abused underage girls in several towns and cities - including Rotherham, Rochdale and Telford, as well as Oxford - between the 1990s and 2010s.

Oxford was one of the places where most of the perpetrators were identified as older men of Pakistani heritage. In some cases, such as in Rotherham, police were accused of hesitating to act out of fear of being seen as racist. But in Oxford a serious case review found no evidence that this had been a factor.

Now, the government has launched a national inquiry to address why vulnerable children were not protected in England and Wales - including whether attitudes to the girls or the ethnicity of the perpetrators contributed to the failings.

News.title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns
News.content:
England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.

The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.

It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.

Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.

Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry, who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".

An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.

That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.

News.title: Key takeaways from BBC interview as Earl Spencer defends claims about King
News.content:
Earl Spencer has told the BBC writing his book about sister Princess Diana, which has made headlines for its criticism of King Charles, was his "duty...as an eyewitness to history".

In an interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg ahead of the memoir's release on Tuesday, Earl Spencer said he wanted "to put things down once and for all that were true".

Among claims made in Swan Song about the King, who was then the Prince of Wales, was that he said "we'll forget her soon enough" during an argument over whether Princes William and Harry should walk in Diana's funeral procession.

In a strongly worded response, Buckingham Palace said the King was "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss".

Here are the key moments from Earl Spencer's interview, which include his first account of how he was told about Diana's death and criticism of press coverage of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

News.title: Watch: Dramatic moment a cargo ship crashes into another vessel
News.content:
Videos circulating on social media appear to show the moment a cargo ship crashes into a fishing vessel, with dramatic footage capturing the impact.

BBC Verify authenticated the clips, identified the ships involved and traced the collision to waters near Singapore, with evidence suggesting it likely happened on 17 September.

It remains unclear whether anyone was injured or killed and why the collision occurred.

News.title: Workers came across human remains – and unearthed a mass grave of 572 people
News.content:
When a mass grave was unearthed in northern Sri Lanka last February, it was not by design.

Workers were digging to extend a cremation ground in the Chemmani area of the Jaffna region when they suddenly discovered human remains, prompting an investigation.

By August, archaeologists had completed the third phase of the excavation at the site, during which they found the skeletal remains of 572 people, including children and infants.

Among the dead were artefacts from their lives â bangles, a school bag, a milk bottle.

It is believed to be the largest mass grave site ever uncovered in Sri Lanka.

There had been whispers of its existence before - a soldier on trial for the rape and murder of a young woman during the country's devastating civil war, had spoken about a mass grave which contained hundreds of bodies. Rights groups said they were disappeared civilians

But there was no proof - until now.

And while the discovery is devastating, it has offered hope to people like Jeyaruby Jeyabalan, whose father was among thousands of people who disappeared during the decades-long war. Jeyabalan and families like his hope that answers about what happened to their loved ones lie among the bodies.

Many Tamils believe the grave holds the victims of extrajudicial killings carried out during the civil war. They are calling for an investigation â and for justice.

But the excavation process at Chemmani has moved slowly, testing the patience of families searching for answers about their disappeared loved ones.

The discovery of hundreds of remains near a previously identified mass grave has fuelled anger among the Tamils, who have long-demanded a thorough inquiry into disappearances.

Many fear the mass grave will eventually fade from public attention because of a lack of political will to pursue the truth â and so the grave has become a rallying point for renewed protests in Sri Lanka's north.

News.title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?
News.content:
There are sensors in every room of Jyoti and Bharat Patel's home. Their movements and habits are monitored constantly.

But this doesn't worry them, in fact it gives them peace of mind.

Jyoti was diagnosed with dementia five years ago, and they are now part of an NHS trial using high-tech devices to help patients live at home safely.

The couple, who are in their 70s, are one of more than 250 families participating in the project by the UK Dementia Research Institute (UK DRI).

The hope is that the technology could be extended more widely across the health service, to reduce preventable trips to hospital and give families peace of mind.

News.title: Temperatures forecast to hit 25C but heatwave chances fall
News.content:
High pressure is building across the UK and this means the weather will become more settled with brighter conditions.

After a chilly start on Monday morning, with sunshine and light winds across much of England and Wales, temperatures will climb into the low 20s.

Even with more cloud in Scotland and Northern Ireland, it will turn warmer with highs also reaching 18 to 22C.

It will also start to feel more humid again.

That more humid air combined with light winds across England and Wales into Tuesday means it will start off rather misty and foggy with areas of low cloud for some.

Once the sun has broken through though, it will feel warmer still.

Temperatures could peak at around 24 or 25C in south-east England, but reach the low 20s Celsius in many other parts of England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Eastern Scotland.

The highest temperature though will be determined by how much the cloud breaks allowing the strong September sunshine through.

2026 has already been a record-breaking year for the number of days above 25C, with last week exceeding the record of 89 days set in 1959.

News.title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting
News.content:
"Donald Trump is trying to claim he's got a success in Greenland, but actually, all he's got is almost a carbon copy of the agreement that's persisted since the 1950s," he said during a Q&A at the Lib Dem party conference.

"So let Donald Trump try to pretend he's had a victory. The truth is, Europe, Nato, countries like Canada stood up to him and won."

Trump had for months threatened to purchase or annex the semi-autonomous territory, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.

Following the announcement of the deal, Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.

The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.

The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.

Burnham has spoken to Trump at least twice since entering Downing Street and No 10 said he intended to use the UNGA to "drive forward work on issues that matter to people at home", including the cost of living and the war in Ukraine.

News.title: Quadruple amputee enters the Big Brother house
News.content:
Charlotte Nott has never let anything hold her back.

The student, from Oxford, is a quadruple amputee, having lost the lower parts of her arms and legs to meningitis when she was just two years old.

Now 18, Charlotte is a contestant in the latest series of Big Brother, something she has dreamed about for most of her life.

Her dad, Alex, told BBC Radio Oxford he was anxious about her appearance on the show, but said there had never been much point telling his daughter not to do something she had her sights on.

That resilience was on full display within seconds of Charlotte's arrival on the show.

During the launch, her shoe broke as she stepped out to be introduced, and she had to remove her prosthetic legs on stage before entering the house.

"Maybe it was my fate to walk in with no legs," she told the diary room. "Maybe that was just what was meant to happen."

She added that she was used to going without her prosthetics at home.

"When I'm at home, I have my legs off all the time," she said. "When I'm cooking, I have my legs off. I like to be four foot. I like to be tiny, like a little tiny doll."

Alex said the moment had summed up his daughter's unstoppable nature perfectly.

News.title: Kelsey Parker welcomes baby after 'devastating' stillbirth last year
News.content:
Kelsey Parker, the widow of The Wanted singer Tom Parker, has welcomed a baby after last year announcing a "devastating" stillbirth.

The podcaster and author, 35, had two children with British boy band star Tom Parker before he died in 2022, aged 33, after being diagnosed with terminal brain cancer.

She is now in a relationship with Will Lindsay and last June revealed the "earth-shattering news" that they had lost their baby Phoenix.

On Sunday, a post on her Instagram account showed a photo of a newborn baby's arm next to a pink sign with the word River. "Welcome to the world, River. Our little bit of hope," the caption said.

Celebrities including The Saturdays singer Rochelle Humes, TV presenter Susanna Reid and reality TV star Holly Hagan-Blyth have congratulated Kelsey Parker on social media.

"Congratulations angel," Rochelle Humes wrote.

"Oh my goodness â this is so wonderful â welcome River," Susanna Reid said.

Hagan-Blyth commented "I am SO happy for you xxxx".

Kelsey Parker's Instagram bio says "turning life's hardest moments into hope".

Last year she posted a poem online after the loss of her stillborn baby.

It was called Born Sleeping, Forever Loved, and began "the world grew quiet as you arrived, So loved, so longed for, yet not alive. Our precious boy, our angel light, Born with wings, took silent flight".

News.title: Homes evacuated over fears fire at seaside hotel weakened building's structure
News.content:
Speaking to the BBC, John Dighton, who was evacuated from Pavilion Court, said that he was told to leave his flat at about 19:00 on Saturday.

The 50-year-old said: "We don't know how long we will be out for but we have grabbed stuff for a couple of days.

"The worst thing is the not knowing. We are at a hotel over the road from the flats."

Ross Honeycomb, 39, was staying at the hotel with his family and told the BBC on Saturday how they were woken by fire alarms at about 01:00.

He said: "I thought I was dreaming, it was horrifying.

"We looked out and there was smoke billowing from the underground car park. Later we started hearing explosions."

Kevin Crawford, 91, and his wife Kathleen, 82, said they had booked in for a two-week stay at the hotel.

The couple, from London, told the BBC that they were in their room on the sixth floor when they heard a fire alarm.

"We saw the fire but we thought the fire brigade had it under control," said Kevin.

"We managed to sleep through it. At the time, we didn't realise how bad the fire was."

The council's chief executive, Susan Priest, said on Saturday: "The extent of support of organisations, including Three Hills, Morrisons and the Salvation Army, has been amazing and helped to ensure that visitors and residents were looked after, supported and had food and hot drinks.

"This was an extremely difficult day, firstly for the hotel guests and this evening for our residents who have had to move out of their homes."

News.title: Billionaire Man United owner loses moral high ground after tax exile, Labour chair says
News.content:
The Labour Party chair has said Sir Jim Ratcliffe loses "the moral high ground" by making statements about the UK while living in tax exile.

Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Bridget Phillipson said she would take the billionaire businessman's comments that the UK was "on the slide" with a "pinch of salt".

Sir Jim, the founder of petrochemical giant Ineos and Manchester United's co-owner, told the BBC he has lost confidence in the UK due to a combination of high taxes and high immigration.

He has been a tax resident in Monaco since 2020 and said "things would have to get better" in the UK for him to return.

When questioned over the remarks, Phillipson said Sir Jim loses "the moral high ground" by "making these kinds of pronouncements while choosing to make decisions, that he is within his rights to make, to become a tax exile".

Pushed on whether it bothers her that people who create jobs and pay a lot of tax were leaving the UK, the minister said she was "optimistic about our country's prospects".

Other high profile billionaires have left the UK, including including steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal and most recently the UK's third biggest taxpayer, hedge-fund boss Chris Rokos.

But, Philipson argued the country was in a good position ahead of the Budget next month, and Andy Burnham has shown a "sense of hope and optimism whilst recognising that many families are still struggling and there is more to do."

"Of course, there are challenges, including big international headwinds, but I fundamentally believe that we are in a strong position going into this budget because of the decisions taken over the last two years, and I believe our country's best days lie ahead of us," she said.

Philipson declined to speculate over whether there would be tax rises in the Budget on 28 October, and said the government remained committed to being disciplined about its spending rules.

News.title: Illegal off-road vehicles to be seized on the spot as police warn of 'long walk home'
News.content:
Police say off-road drivers causing anti-social behaviour or damage to protected habitats will have their vehicles seized "on the spot".

PC Eryl Lloyd, of North Wales Police's rural crime team, said new powers allowed officers to take vehicles without notice, and warned offending drivers: "It's a long walk home."

Both the force and Natural Resources Wales (NRW) said damage caused by off-roading incidents and other anti-social behaviour was on the rise.

In August, three men who caused "irreversible" harm to the Berwyn Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in 4x4s were convicted after videos of them causing the damage were shared on TikTok.

John Robinson, Michael Williams and Joseph Hodgson were part of a seven-vehicle convoy which drove from Liverpool to the Berwyn range - an area of moorland in northeast Wales - where they caused "serious damage" to the peat and bog habitat.

Robinson and Williams were fined more than Â£2,000 each and disqualified from driving for two months. Hodgson was ordered to pay Â£1,000 compensation for damaging the SSSI, as well as costs, and was also banned from entering the Berwyn SSSI for three years.

Lloyd - who is seconded to NRW - said his team had "definitely seen an increase in off-roading incidents".

As well as 4x4 vehicles and motorbikes, "we're getting a lot more reports about e-bikes, which also cause the same amount of damage as motorbikes", he added.

News.title: Tens of thousands of fridge freezers left at docks as household collections suspended
News.content:
People have reported storing broken fridges and freezers in their gardens for months because some council collections have been suspended.

It follows the closure of specialist treatment facilities and a wider shortage of capacity to process cooling appliances, the Local Government Authority (LGA) said.

Recycling company Unimetals, which had dozens of sites in the UK, filed for liquidation in 2025 leaving tens of thousands of fridge freezers at Newport Docks.

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it was working to manage the capacity shortages.

Almost a quarter of Welsh councils say they have suspended household collections of fridge-freezers due to a shortage of space at disposal sites.

Cardiff is one of these and Lee Young, who lives in the city, has been trying to get rid of his broken fridge-freezer for two months.

"I tried to take it to the recycling centre in July but was told it wasn't accepted. Someone said the council would collect it, but they won't either."

It has been sitting in his back garden ever since and he does not know when council collections will resume.

Paramount and California's attorney general have engaged in advanced discussions over potential concessions to settle a major antitrust challenge, according to a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday citing sources familiar with the matter.

The proposed terms reportedly include a $1.5 billion commitment to film and television production within the state.

The lawsuit, brought by California alongside 11 other states, remains a key remaining obstacle to Paramount’s planned $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

open image in gallery Paramount and California's attorney general have discussed a range of concessions in advanced ​settlement negotiations ( Reuters )

State regulators moved to block the transaction in July, arguing that merging the two companies would create a dominant media entity with the power to inflate prices across film and television markets.

Alongside the production investment, negotiators have discussed commitments requiring Paramount to retain its studio lots and maintain its primary operations within California, according to the report.

Enforcement mechanisms are also under consideration if Paramount fails to fulfill a previous pledge to produce 30 theatrical films per year following the merger. Penalties could require the company to divest its stake in Miramax, the studio behind acclaimed releases such as "No Country for Old Men" and "Pulp Fiction."

Further provisions being weighed include divesting certain cable television channels and creating an oversight board designed to protect CNN's editorial independence.

open image in gallery . Penalties could require the company to divest its stake in Miramax, the studio behind acclaimed releases such as "No Country for Old Men" and "Pulp Fiction” ( Getty )

In response to inquiries, a spokesperson for the California AG said in a statement to Reuters: "Potential settlement talks are confidential.

We cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their alleged substance." Representatives for Paramount Skydance did not immediately respond to requests for comment submitted outside standard business hours.

A settlement between Paramount and the states could be finalized as early as this weekend, with terms expected to address theatrical release guarantees and independent monitoring of CNN, Reuters reported last week.

The deal is a cornerstone of Paramount CEO David Ellison's strategy, who sees the consolidation of two iconic Hollywood studios and their combined television assets as crucial to the company's future growth.

Cole Palmeris set to withdrawn from the England squad, with Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo also doubts to join up with Thomas Tuchel‘s camp.

Palmer, who was recalled by Tuchel last week after he was left out of England’s squad for the World Cup, is reportedly dealing with a small muscle injury, though he completed Chelsea’s 3-0 defeat to Brentford on Friday night.

The 24-year-old has featured in all five of Chelsea’s Premier League matches this term but struggled with injuries in a disrupted campaign last season, recently saying during a Twitch stream that he “had one leg for 10 months”.

Cole Palmer has withdrawn from England’s squad ahead of the start of the Nations League ( Getty )

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick confirmed Rashford picked up an “issue” when during the 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday, with the forward substituted while appearing to be struggling with his hip – which was a persistent issue over the summer.

Midfielder Mainoo, who travelled to this summer’s World Cup but did not play a single minute of the tournament under Tuchel, was also substituted during the closing stages of the draw at Craven Cottage.

England will play four matches over the newly expanded three-week international break, kicking off against World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday 26 September. That is followed by trips to Czech Republic and Croatia, before concluding the set of Nations League games against the Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday 6 October.

Palmer has started the season in excellent form, with four goals and two assists in seven appearances in all competitions while establishing a dangerous partnership with Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro, who has withdrawn from Brazil’s squad due to injury.

Chelsea do not return to Premier League action until Saturday 10 October with a home game against Bournemouth, giving Xabi Alonso’s side three weeks to manage Palmer’s injury over the international window.

News.title: ‘Worst guard dog’: Golden retriever pesters home intruder to play during break-in
News.content:
A golden retriever pestered a home intruder to play during a break-in in San Diego, California, security video shows.

Homeowner Dante Rowley said he and his family watched the incident unfold in real-time remotely through their home cameras as they were boarding a flight.

Instead of chasing the man away, the family's dog Nash was keen to make friends, bringing the individual his toys.

When police arrived at the door, the pooch appeared to believe they were there for one reason – playtime.

"Nash is the worst guard dog," Rowley wrote.

Footage from outside the house shows police officers placing the man in handcuffs.

Strictly Come Dancing may be a thing of the past for Claudia Winkleman, but she’s thrown her support behind the new era of the BBC series.

The revamped show started on Saturday (19 September) with a pre-recorded launch episode in which new hosting trio Emma Willis, Johannes Radebe and Josh Widdicombe made their debut, and the pairings for this year’s series were revealed.

Winkleman herself approved of Willis’ hiring and shared an encouraging response when the former Big Brother and Voice UK presenter showcased her outfit of choice for the launch show.

open image in gallery Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe are ‘Strictly’s new hosts ( BBC )

Ahead of the episode’s broadcast, Willis wrote on Instagram: “Week one… I guess it’s officially happening then. Dress on, game face ready and fully prepared for the glitter to take over…Strictly, let’s be having you.”

The following day, Traitors presenter Winkleman replied “knockout” with four heart emojis.

At one stage in Willis, Radebe and Widdicombe’s first Strictly episode, Emmerdale star Lawrence Robb told the new hosts he feels he has “large shoes to fill” after the success of his fellow soap stars Kelvin Fletcher and Lewis Cope on the show in previous years, adding: “I guess I can empathise with you guys, filling Claudia and Tess’ boots.”

Tess Daly and Winkleman quit the series in October 2025. While they did not disclose their reason for stepping down at the time, Winkleman revealed months later that it had nothing to do with the scandals that rocked the show in recent years, but instead stemmed from their mutual feeling that the show needed some new faces.

“It occurred to both of us about a year before,” she told MailOnline. “The show deserves new. We wanted to leave when we were on an absolute high.”

open image in gallery Claudia Winkleman supports new 'Strictly' host Emma Willis ( Instagram )

When asked if her decision had anything to do with the scandal surrounding Giovanni Pernice and Amanda Abbington, which prompted a review into the professional dancers’ behind-the-scenes behaviour, the presenter said: “Absolutely not.”

She continued: “It is a genuinely beautiful show to be part of. Almost every single person who’s taken part is happy they did. So no, it wasn’t that.”

Winkleman said that after she and Daly filmed their final piece to camera in the latest series’s live final, she went to her husband, film producer Kris Thykier, and sobbed over the “momentous” exit. “It was 20 years of my life,” she added.

Winkleman and Daly, 56, received a special message from Queen Camilla during their final live episode in December 2025. Read aloud by judge Craig Revel Horwood, she said the pair’s “warmth, compassion and sheer happiness” had been at the core of the show’s success.

“I think I speak for everyone when I say you have been utterly fab-u-lous,” the Queen’s message said.

Daly began presenting the show 21 years ago alongside the late Sir Bruce Forsyth, while Winkleman joined her in 2014, having hosted Strictly’s sister show It Takes Two since 2004.

Winkleman will now be kept busy presenting The Traitors and its celebrity spin-off, as well as her very own BBC chat show, which is set to launch in March.

News.title: UK urged to ‘team up’ with EU and Canada in economic partnership
News.content:

Britain should "team up" with Canada and the EU economically, the Canadian finance minister has said, arguing closer partnerships are needed in the face of a changing global political landscape.

Francois-Philippe Champagne said the countries shared a similar “vision” of the world, arguing they are “stronger together”.

It comes after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen earlier this month proposed Canada join the European bloc as an “associate member”.

The proposed associate status does not exist under EU treaties, with Canadian prime minister Mark Carney acknowledging its role is yet to be defined.

Calling for closer ties with Britain, alongside the EU, Mr Champagne told the BBC: “We need to look at partnership in a different way, and the great thing is that when you look at Canada, and I would say the United Kingdom, we share the same values.

open image in gallery Francois-Philippe Champagne ( Reuters )

“We are very aligned in our vision of the world. Why don’t we team up? We are independent and sovereign, but we are stronger together.”

Talking about Canada’s future role as an “associate member”, Mr Champagne said: “This is all about the substance, to build an alliance of the future.

“The world has changed. America has changed. So we need to change.”

Ties between traditional allies Canada and the United States have strained under Donald Trump, after the president threatened to make the country the 51st American state and imposed hefty tariffs on Canadian goods.

Canada has been seeking to diversify its economic relationships amid heightened tensions.

But announcing the planned cooperation, Ms von der Leyen was careful to state that “this is a partnership not against anyone else” in a possible effort to avoid antagonising the US president.

Mr Trump has yet to respond to the burgeoning relationship, but he has clashed with Canada and its leadership repeatedly in recent months.

open image in gallery Tensions between Canada and the US have been rising in recent months ( AFP/Getty )

Prime minister Andy Burnham is expected to meet with US President Donald Trump at the UN General Assembly in New York this week, having spoken to each other at least twice on the phone since Mr Burnham entered Downing Street in July.

Mr Carney previously told the European Parliament he welcomed deeper ties in defence, trade, financial services, energy and artificial intelligence, but he later clarified that Canada would not be seeking full EU membership.

“We do not seek power to dominate others,” added the former Bank of England governor.

“On the contrary, we are pursuing resilience so that no one can control our open markets, impair our sovereignty, threaten our territorial integrity, or undermine our freedoms, our democracies, our rule of law.”

In August, Mr Trump signed an order to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America”, claimed that Canada “is the worst to deal with on trade” and suggested the US defends its neighbour while getting nothing in return.

Mr Carney, in turn, has claimed the Trump administration is trying to “break us so America can own us” and vowed to “never forget the lessons” of what he termed the “American betrayal”. He has pledged to double Canada’s non-US trade in the next decade.

Celebrity hairdresser Chris Appleton has suggested his friend and client Kim Kardashian could be cheering him on from the studio audience as he takes part in Strictly Come Dancing.

The 43-year-old was paired with professional dancer Amy Dowden on Saturday’s launch episode of the BBC One entertainment show.

He will compete against stars including singer Delta Goodrem, former Love Island winner Dani Dyer and former England footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips.

Asked if Kardashian, whose reality TV show The Kardashians has featured Appleton, would attend a live show, he said: "Who knows? Watch this space, but I don’t know, anything could happen.

"I think being in Strictly, I’ve realised anything is possible and magic happens.

"I have no idea, I know a lot of people want to come to the show and we’re only allocated two tickets."

It comes after Kardashian posted on social media to support Appleton when his participation in the show was announced and also sent him flowers.

open image in gallery Kim Kardashian and North West present the award to Chris Appleton, Hair Artist of the Year Award recipient, onstage during The Daily Front Row's Seventh Annual Fashion Los Angeles Awards ( Getty )

The Leicester-born hairdresser added: “Kim’s so sweet, I mean, she’s been such an amazing person throughout my whole career.

“She’s obviously fantastic at what she does, but obviously I know Kim personally, and she’s just always been so kind, and she sent me a beautiful bouquet of flowers, which was just so kind of her to do, she didn’t have to.

“And she said, ‘break a leg’, and just commenting on my post when I did it, and that’s so nice of her to support me because she’s always been so supportive.

“But to do that, which is going above and beyond, it just says so much about who she is, she’s an amazing person.

“Like I say, she’s always been so supportive, I’m very lucky to work with her, and she’s my hair muse, she’s always been my girl.”

open image in gallery The hair stylist – who is best known for working with stars including Kim Kardashian and Jennifer Lopez – said he was counting down to appearing in the BBC series ( PA )

Appleton’s other celebrity clients include Sofía Vergara, Ariana Grande and Katy Perry.

He has previously been named a “Hair Star” by Vogue UK and his work has been showcased on covers and in major features for publications including Vogue, Harper’s Bazaar, Vanity Fair, Marie Claire, Grazia, L’Officiel Paris, and more.

The hair stylist also recently made the New York Times Best Sellers list for his memoir Your Roots Don’t Define You.

Appleton will return to Strictly in Saturday’s first live show on BBC One and iPlayer at 6.15pm.

Chancellor John Healey will face pressure to raise taxes or cut spending at next month’s Budget, as soaring borrowing costs because of the Iran war and weaker growth has wiped nearly £12 billion off the Government’s fiscal headroom, according to a new report.

The latest KPMG economic outlook estimates that Mr Healey could be left with headroom of about £12 billion in the autumn, down from £23.6 billion at the time of the spring forecast.

It said rising borrowing costs on the UK’s debt after the Middle East conflict has already cut about £9 billion off the headroom, with sluggish growth and expected downgrades from the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) likely to to reduce it by about another £2 billion.

KPMG said: “The Chancellor will have limited scope to provide significant support for growth or the cost of living when the Budget is delivered next month, as higher borrowing costs and weaker growth have reduced the Government’s fiscal headroom.

“Restoring the previous level of headroom could require tax rises or spending reductions.

“With the Government committed to not increasing taxes on working people, the Chancellor may need to consider other tax measures.”

Long-term borrowing costs have been surging amid a gilt sell-off driven by inflation worries caused by the Iran war and rising expectations of a rise in interest rates by the year end.

These factors will combine to leave Mr Healey with “limited room for manoeuvre” at his October 28 inaugural Budget, KPMG said.

The group is predicting UK interest rates will likely rise in November, from 3.75% to 4%, but then start falling back next summer as the impact of energy prices on inflation fades away.

It is forecasting inflation, which rose to 3.1% in August, will rise to about 3.5% in the autumn and peak at about 4% in the first quarter of next year.

KPMG is pencilling in growth of 1.3% overall in 2026, but with slower growth in the final six months as inflation weighs on household spending.

Growth will edge up to 1.4% next year, according to the group.

News.title: Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change
News.content:
But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.

He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

News.title: Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool
News.content:
It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The record books will show that this meeting, a proper Test full of ebbs and flows, was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level of professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

“The plan on the field at the last scrum was to go for the win,” Canada captain Sophie de Goede said. “And then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. In that moment you have to trust your coach and your coaching staff, and we’ll have a discussion about it later. If we had given away a penalty off the next breakdown, we’d be sitting here going, ‘Why didn’t you kick it out?’”

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance, in a tale which was not too dissimilar to last week. The hosts came second in the physical battle, too, which was uncharacteristic of them; losing Hannah Botterman to a shoulder injury did not help, either. All told, Canada just looked as though they wanted it a little bit more and maybe this was the wake-up call the Red Roses needed: when you are at the top, and at the top by a margin, every team want to be the one to dethrone you.

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

Sports.content:

COLE PALMER is set to pull out of the England squad in a major blow to Thomas Tuchel.

The Chelsea star, 24, only just won his place back in the Three Lions squad after being snubbed by Tuchel for the World Cup.



But according to the Athletic, Palmer is withdrawing ahead of Nations League games against Spain, Croatia and Czechia.

Palmer’s absence is due to “load management” after playing nearly every minute of Chelsea’s 2026-27 season so far.



He played the entire 90 minutes of Chelsea’s 3-0 loss to Brentford on Friday night.

Fans will have been excited to see Palmer back in an England shirt after a promising start to the season with the Blues.



He has four goals and two assists in all competitions and has combined well with England team-mate Morgan Rogers.

But his shot at redemption for the Three Lions will go on after being left out of Tuchel’s 26-man group for the 2026 World Cup.

That snub followed a disappointing 2025-26 campaign for Palmer that saw him score just ten goals and register one assist.

The report also claims Manchester United star Kobbie Mainoo is also “likely” to pull out after picking up an injury in their 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim admits to Man Utd ‘mistakes’ with AC Milan manager fearing history is repeating itself
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Manchester United head coach Ruben Amorim has admitted to making “mistakes” at Old Trafford and says he is learning from them with AC Milan.

Amorim continued his unbeaten start to the Serie A season at the weekend with a 3-0 win over Lecce.



It left AC Milan fifth in the table with 11 points from five games.

The 41-year-old admitted after the match that giving the players more freedom was the key to victory.



He also said it was a learning curve from his time at Man Utd.

Reflecting on the performance, Amorim explained: “I think we improved a lot. The freedom in the players, the movement, especially the runs behind, so we are not just a team that has the ball, we are a team that is dangerous.

“We have space to run into and that is a good thing. We controlled the game, we understood the opposition were waiting for our mistake, but we defended quite well and deserved the win.”

Asked what sparked the change, he continued: “It’s an observation of the games and the characteristics.

“Of course I listen to the players, but a manager especially in a big team is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every players wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.

“It’s always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.

“Sometimes we don’t have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don’t have it, we have to adapt.

“I think today worked, in another game we can return to the build-up with three, the important thing is to have different ways of playing.

“That’s especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lost the reference of what we want to do, it’s harder for them to understand the mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams.”

Amorim is the first coach since Nils Liedholm in 1963 to pick up 11 points in his opening five Serie A games.

“It’s a good statistic, but this is a different time,” he said. “We have a lot to do, but we are improving and we are learning.



“We had difficulties in the last games, because the structure was really blocked in the positions, but the players had a little more freedom, and they played better with a little more freedom.”

Amorim managed seven points from his opening five games with Man Utd last season.

He was then sacked in January, ending his 14-month stay at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Forgotten England star, 26, scores sublime solo goal against PSG just days after squad announcement
Sports.content:
Next

A FORGOTTEN England star scored a sublime solo goal just days after the latest squad announcement.

Thomas Tuchel named his 27-man list of players for the upcoming Nations League games against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.



And one man gave the perfect response to being overlooked once again.

Angel Gomes earned all four of his senior England caps in 2024 under interim boss Lee Carsley – and has not featured under Tuchel.



So while his name was not mentioned among those unfortunate or surprised to miss out for this extended international break, the midfielder still showed what he can do.

The Marseille midfielder, 26, came off the bench for his Ligue 1 side during today’s clash with PSG at the Stade Velodrome.

And he made a big impact with the equaliser – and did it in style, too.

Gomes collected the ball on the counter attack on the edge of the PSG penalty area.

He then chopped inside, bamboozling Willian Pacho, before poking the ball beyond Matvey Safonov into the back of the net.

That goal came in a crazy 11-minute second-half spell.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Ferran Torres opened the scoring for PSG on 66 minutes, Gomes levelled it up six minutes later but Marquinhos restored the visitors’ lead two minutes later – then Timothy Weah got sent off in the 77th minute.

The result condemned Marseille to a fifth defeat on the spin.

But even so, plenty of the talk on social media was about Gomes’ individual brilliance.

One said: “Fantastic finish.”



Another wrote: “A moment of magic.”

A third added: “What a stunner.”

And a final user typed: “Perfect.”



Gomes came through the academy at Manchester United and made ten first-team appearances before moving to France, initially with Lille in 2020.

He signed for Marseille last year but spent the second half of last season on loan at Wolves, unable to keep them up.

Sports.title: Newcastle star Lewis Hall reveals he was shocked and heartbroken at England World Cup snub
Sports.content:
Next

LEWIS HALL was heartbroken and shocked to be left out of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad.

The left-back, 22, celebrated his England recall this week with the winner in Newcastle’s 2-1 victory over Hull City.



The Toon star, who has penned a new contract until 2031, heads off for Three Lions duty with a point to prove having been forced to frustratingly watch this summer’s action back home with his mates.

Hall said: “Yeah, I was gutted. In football, you never take anything for granted, but I’d say I wasn’t necessarily expecting it, if I’m being completely honest. Obviously everyone has their own opinions and you’ve got to respect that.



“But as soon as the first couple of weeks were done, when I realised I wasn’t going to be there, I just had to think to myself that if I wasn’t a footballer, what would I be doing, and that’s supporting England.

“So I was just with my mates watching the games together and just being a fan.”



While it was misery for Hall, a host of current and former Newcastle team-mates did get the nod from Tuchel.

Hall said: “I was obviously supporting all of them with Dan [Burn] being there, Elliot [Anderson], Anthony [Gordon], and big Tino [Livramento].

“I was obviously buzzing for them and wanted all of them to do so well. So, when I was watching them and they were all playing really well, it obviously made me proud as well.

“So I was looking at it that way.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Hall now hopes to show Tuchel exactly what he missed in the upcoming Nations League league clashes with Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if he had an extra point to prove, he said: “A little bit. You play enough games in a season anyways where they can see how you play, see what you’re good at, can improve on and how you fit into the squad.

“It’s always nice to go there and create a good impression. I’ll be looking to do that. I’m just looking forward to meeting up with everyone again, because it’s been a while.”

Hall at least knows that he will not be as busy as he has been in the opening weeks of the season. Despite Newcastle’s run of one defeat in five in the Prem, they have conceded a whopping 96 shots – with 22 of those coming against Hull.



On that worrying stat, he added: “It’s not nice. We know that that’s something we need to improve on. It’s difficult today, cause I felt like the first 60 minutes we didn’t feel like conceding at all, and then they get one chance and all of a sudden the game changes.

“That’s something that we’re looking at and trying to improve on. But yeah, it sounds like a lot.

“I’d love to see how it compares to everyone else before I comment on it, but it’s not really what you want to hear. You don’t want to be facing shots as a defender, but at the same time, it’s our job as well as the midfielders and the goalkeeper to be able to stop these shots and block them.



“We’re trying every day to improve our defensive work.”

Hall produced another stellar display to help keep Hull at bay. Manager Matthias Jaissle, who went viral after the game for buying a Toon fan’s birthday meal after bumping into the party at a city restaurant, cannot wait to see what more the player can contribute to his team.

He said: “He’s such a talented player, really focused, really committed. When you look at the statistics, he’s probably already at the same numbers compared to the whole last season.

“He’s doing an amazing job, and he has a bright, bright future.”

Sports.title: Man Utd run SIX KILOMETRES less than Fulham with Carrick’s men looking Premier League’s worst team without ball
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED players ran over SIX KILOMETRES less than their Fulham counterparts on Sunday.

Red Devils boss Michael Carrick insisted there was nothing wrong with the urgency and effort from his players in the 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage.



But club legend Gary Neville called United a “genuine disgrace“.

And the statistics back up the Sky Sports pundit rather than the man in the Old Trafford hot seat.



According to data collected by FotMob, United players collectively covered 110.2km – a full 6.5km less than Fulham‘s 116.7km.

Look into the other running metrics and it becomes even more worrying for Carrick.

Fulham covered a greater distance running, sprinting, and made 10 more overall sprints than their opponents.

Carrick could have been under serious pressure had Matheus Cunha not salvaged a draw with his deflected 89th-minute strike.

But he is by no means out of the woods after a flat performance and dropped points against a side who have not won in the Premier League all season.

SunSport Manchester United reporter Katherine Walsh said: “United are quite possibly the worst side in the Premier League at the moment out of possession.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“They were outworked, outmuscled, and were effectively accused of walking around the pitch by Gary Neville in his post-match interview as well as on commentary.

“Us in the press box, we couldn’t quite believe what we were watching after half-time – the lack of effort, the disjointedness as well. So that is a real problem.”

Carrick now has an extended international break to ponder his next move.



And Neville sent him a stern warning on Sky Sports, ranting: “Very rarely do I say a team doesn’t work hard or is lacking in effort. That’s the ultimate criticism you can give a group of players.

“I’m always very careful to say that, but in those first 15 minutes of that second half, and generally for the first 60 minutes, Man Utd were a genuine disgrace. Nowhere near good enough without the ball.

“Michael is of course saying something different to us than he is saying privately. That would’ve really worried me.



“People will ask questions about him, but he knew that when he took the job.

“But there’s no panic in that sense – no one is putting pressure on Carrick – but if those types of performances continue, he will find himself in a lot of trouble. They’ve got to work harder than that for him.”

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee astonished as Elliot Anderson gets away with SLAPPING ball in penalty box against Sunderland
Sports.content:
Next

ELLIOT ANDERSON was “fortunate” to get away with slapping the ball in the penalty box, according to a former Premier League referee.

The £116million midfielder appeared to knock the ball away with his hand during a tussle with Enzo Le Fee.



And as Sunderland ace Le Fee appealed desperately to the referee, Anderson booted it clear to safety.

The incident happened when the bonkers Etihad blockbuster remained in the balance at 3-2 to Enzo Maresca’s side.



Mark Halsey believes the VAR at Stockley Park should have intervened.

That is because he reckons the Black Cats were unequivocally hard done by – as Anderson made an intentional movement towards the ball.

And had VAR stepped in, it could have had a major impact on the result – just like the blunder to allow Erling Haaland’s winner to stand in the Manchester derby last week.

SunSport’s Halsey said: “Sunderland should have had a second-half penalty against Manchester City.

“When City led 3-2, Enzo Le Fee and Elliot Anderson challenged for a ball in the box.

“The latter deliberately moved his arm towards the ball and slapped it away.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I am amazed Michael Salisbury on VAR did not recommend referee Rob Jones for a review.

“City were fortunate to get away with that and then Antoine Semenyo made it 4-2 minutes later.”

That was Semenyo’s second of the afternoon.

Within two minutes, though, Brian Brobbey scored his third to make it 4-3 before Haaland wrapped up the three points – and has now found the net against all the Premier League teams he has faced.

However, much of social media was fixated on the Anderson incident – and most agreed with Halsey, although some suggested the other replay angle was less conclusive.



One blasted: “Elliot Anderson literally slaps the ball away… and that’s not a penalty?! Another VAR howler. What are we even doing anymore?”

Another fumed: “Wow, missed that one live. That’s damming.”

A third moaned: “That’s crazy? I don’t even understand the rules any more.”

And a final user joked: “VAR needs to be taken off air.”

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher speaks his mind on Florian Wirtz in damning verdict on Liverpool struggles
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher speaks his mind on Florian Wirtz in damning verdict on Liverpool struggles

Jamie Carragher has branded Florian Wirtz's display against Bournemouth as one of the worst he's ever seen in a Liverpool shirt

View Image Liverpool's Florian Wirtz was criticised for his display against Bournemouth (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has delivered a damning verdict on Florian Wirtz and urged Andoni Iraola to leave the Liverpool star out against Manchester City. While the Reds secured a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon courtesy of Alexander Isak's strike, Carragher reckons Wirtz delivered his most underwhelming display in a Liverpool shirt at the Vitality Stadium.

‌



Speaking on commentary, he said: "Wirtz has been really poor again. It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all."

‌



And then, during a dedicated Sky Sports podcast following the match, the former Liverpool defender expanded on his assessment of the German: "That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt.

‌



Liverpool news: Victor Munoz reveals surprise as Reds star told to show he deserves new deal READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher talks up two Liverpool transfers who could follow Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

"But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is. And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago.

"And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head. I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game it was what I've seen for the last 12 months.

‌



"I don't see how he's going to hurt you. It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid. The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low.

"Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League. The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big.

"You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting. And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't."

‌



Wirtz will now join up with the Germany squad for the forthcoming Nations League fixtures, before the Reds resume their campaign against City on Sunday, October 11.

Carragher is absolutely certain that the attacking midfielder has no place in Liverpool's starting lineup when they face City at Anfield. He added: "I think going forward Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.

"I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn't produce [against Bournemouth], he's then going to have a three-week break.

‌

"By the time we come back, we're into October. Before you know it, it'll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it'll feel like we're getting to Christmas. He has to do something! If you go through the Premier League and think of players in his position - not just for the top teams, forget the top teams who we should be judging him against, I'm talking about normal Premier League players in the middle of the table - who have done more for their clubs.

"I think of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall at Everton. No one out there would say Dewsbury-Hall is a better player than Wirtz, or would go for more money than Wirtz, or would cost £120m. But every three or four weeks he scores a goal. I watched Morgan Gibbs-White for Nottingham Forest last week at Aston Villa, and in the second half he put in a performance in 45 minutes that Florian Wirtz has never done before for Liverpool.

"I've seen a goal Emiliano Buendia scored for Aston Villa at Tottenham. Again, these players aren't going to get over £100m, or £120m, but they're still giving their clubs bits every few weeks. Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team.

"The things I've liked so far about Iraola, he's had the courage to make big decisions. Ryan Gravenberch has just signed a hefty contract on a five-year deal on massive money, because they thought him and Szoboszlai were going to be the future of the midfield going forward. He's not playing.

The full-back situation, he keeps changing the full-backs, he's dropped Jeremie Frimpong straight away. Milos Kerkez has been in and out. So he's made decisions.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney makes brutal admission about management future – 'I knew that would probably be it'
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney makes brutal admission about management future – 'I knew that would probably be it'

Wayne Rooney confessed his stance on his managerial career

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney's most recent managerial post lasted just seven months (Image: PA)

Wayne Rooney admitted he knew failure at Plymouth Argyle would likely end his future in management. The Manchester United legend was appointed Plymouth boss in May 2024 after a disappointing three-month spell at Birmingham City, which culminated in his sacking at St Andrews.

The 40-year-old was in it for the long haul at Home Park, having signed a three-year contract. However, his time at the club ended in disaster as he was dismissed after just seven months in charge, leaving the now-League One club bottom of the Championship.

His stint at Plymouth remains his last managerial post. He has since taken on major roles in punditry and podcasting, leaving his future in coaching uncertain. Speaking to The Guardian ahead of the Disney+ TV series: The Real Rooneys, the former England captain knew he'd likely leave management if he didn't succeed with Plymouth.

‌



He said: "I was at a crossroads. Up till then my whole career had been playing or coaching. I knew if Plymouth didn’t pay off that would probably be my last management job. And when it didn’t pay off I had to come to terms with my future probably not being in the dugout."

When asked whether he found it difficult to accept that venturing into management had been a failure, he answered: "No, I think I’ve always been good at accepting things.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Wayne Rooney reveals he quit booze and shares raw feelings with Coleen after 'pressure' built up READ MORE :

"Like when I moved from Man United back to Everton, I accepted quickly that I’m not the level anymore to play for Man United, so you’re coming down again. So I’ve been quite good at not hanging round too long, because I’ve seen players play for too long.

"After Plymouth, it was tough, there’s no denying that." Rooney has since become a regular on TV screens with The Wayne Rooney Show on the BBC, while co-hosting the new Disney+ show Stick to United with YouTuber Mark Goldbridge.

View 2 Images The Man Utd icon has become a major player in punditry (Image: Photo by Isabelle Field/Plymouth Argyle via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Rooney is also set to host the new BBC show 'Can You Beat Wayne Rooney?' alongside comedian Alex Brooker and is reportedly nearing a mammoth deal to appear on ITV hit show I'm A Celebrity.

His potential appearance in the jungle would come two years after his wife, Coleen, finished runner-up to McFly singer Danny Jones. The former footballer is reportedly keen to impress his four sons, Kai, 16, Klay, 13, Kit, 10, and Cass, eight, by showing his mettle in the Bushtucker Trials.
