Sports.title: Man Utd news: Michael Carrick reacts to apology as he's told whole season hinges on one star
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick reacts to apology as he's told whole season hinges on one star

Manchester United and Michael Carrick head into the international break looking to catch their breath after weeks of turmoil and chaos both on and off the pitch

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has reacted to an apology (Image: Getty)

It's hasn't exactly been an ideal start to the new season for Manchester United. Results and performances on the pitch have been inconsistent, while off it, the club has had plenty to contend with.

‌



Injuries have disrupted Michael Carrick's plans, with marquee summer signing Carlos Baleba forced to wait weeks for his debut after arriving at United last month. VAR controversies have added to the frustration, while the situation surrounding academy starlet JJ Gabriel has provided another unwanted distraction.

‌



The 15-year-old is reportedly pushing to leave United, despite the club viewing him as a potential first-team player in the future. Taken together, it has made for a particularly eventful opening few weeks at Old Trafford.

‌



Now, though, the first international break of the season offers United an opportunity to take stock and regroup before domestic football resumes next month. With that in mind, here are the latest Manchester United headlines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Coleen Rooney reveals what husband Wayne is really like as she names four key traits READ MORE :

Carrick reacts to Pro Ref apology

Michael Carrick has played down the significance of the apology Manchester United received from Pro Ref, formerly known as PGMOL, after a VAR error allowed Manchester City's winner in the Manchester derby to stand.

‌



Pro Ref chief Howard Webb admitted an officiating mistake had been made after Erling Haaland's decisive goal was allowed to stand despite City team-mate Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position. The goal had initially been ruled out before a VAR review overturned the on-field decision.

The decision immediately attracted scrutiny, with questions raised over how Fernandez's position had not been taken into account during the review. An apology was subsequently issued to United shortly after the final whistle.

View 3 Images Erling Haaland's goal against Man Utd was controversially allowed to stand (Image: Getty)

‌



Carrick remains supportive of VAR but admits the apology did little to ease his frustration over what happened. "Listen, one-off things can happen," he said. "I've got faith in [the system] of course... [but] the apology doesn't mean an awful lot.

"I can appreciate it and I respect them for putting their hands up and saying 'we got that wrong'. It happens. Moving forward, we just have to deal with what's thrown in front of us."

Man Utd told season 'hinges on Baleba'

Former Manchester United striker Louis Saha believes the club's season could hinge on whether Carlos Baleba can step into the void left by Casemiro and establish himself as their new midfield anchor.

‌



Baleba joined United from Brighton for £70million this summer and is expected to take over as the side's first-choice No. 6. Casemiro had occupied that role for several years before leaving Old Trafford, and Saha believes Baleba has the attributes to fill his predecessor's shoes.

However, the Frenchman has warned that United need Baleba to hit the ground running, arguing that his ability to drive the team forward could be crucial to unlocking their attacking players.

View 3 Images Louis Saha thinks Carlos Baleba will be key for Man Utd this season (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"Manchester United's season will only truly begin once Carlos Baleba is fit enough to be the starting, first-choice midfielder in the team," the Frenchman said. "He brings more power to the game than Kobbie Mainoo or Youri Tielemans, who are both great footballers, but Baleba has a greater engine and can take this team to a higher level.

"I like how aggressive he can be with the ball, and I think he can drive forward to break the lines with his dribbling. It would be a mistake to put him into a system that stops him doing that. "He can be like Casemiro, who was not a dribbler but he was able to get the team up the pitch and play passes high to the striker or the wingers straight away. He recovered the ball and his first pass was always forward. Sometimes he made mistakes or lost the ball but it doesn't matter because the benefit to the team compensated that. "This is the job of the defence to give their midfielders the confidence to take these risks and find other players. If they don't feel they can take these risks, it is a great shame because right now Manchester United have a forward line of real killers.

"They just aren’t being given the freedom to play. Carlos Baleba can give them that freedom and unlock the team more than Kobbie Mainoo or Youri Tielemans but they can provide that balance. You need both."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta points the finger as Bruno Guimaraes told he's 'miles off it'
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta points the finger as Bruno Guimaraes told he's 'miles off it'

Arsenal will head into the international break licking their wounds after suffering a 3-0 defeat to Brighton on Saturday afternoon in the Premier League

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal were demolished by Brighton 3-0 (Image: Getty)

Arsenal's unbeaten start to the season came to an abrupt end on Saturday as they were defeated by Brighton. Gunners fans will have to stew on that for three weeks as the Premier League goes on hiatus for an extended international break.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side had begun their Premier League title defence perfectly, winning their first four top-flight games against Coventry City, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Sunderland. They also downed Napoli in the Champions League and eased past Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup third round.

‌



However, their trip to the South Coast ended in disaster as their nine-match league win streak was snapped. Goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres condemned Arsenal to a 3-0 defeat at the Amex.

‌



Arteta will now have some time to digest the club's first loss of the season, but in the immediate aftermath, he pointed the finger at his players. A Gunners legend has also hit out at Bruno Guimaraes as Mirror Football brings you all the latest from the Emirates.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd, Liverpool and Chelsea have questions to answer in best of the rest race READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa in agreement over 'unacceptable' Arsenal defeat READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta's finger pointing

Before Saturday, Arsenal hadn't conceded three goals in a game since a December 2023 4-3 victory over Luton Town. Arteta blamed his players after the Brighton match, claiming they were error-ridden.

‌



View 3 Images Arteta was not pleased after losing to the Seagulls (Image: Getty)

He said: "Brighton deserved to win the game. We didn't do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn't win enough duels and any second balls and that stretches you. With the errors that we made and especially with the principles we didn't apply against a team that wants to press you.

‌



"So that puts us constantly under pressure and didn't get out of that in the way we normally do. So a lot of things to learn and take, but ultimately disappointed."

Paul Merson critiques Bruno Guimaraes

Summer signing Guimaraes started next to Declan Rice in the heart of midfield against Brighton, but endured a torrid time of things. He was replaced after 60 minutes by Mikel Merino and admitted post-match that it was a bad day at the office.

View 3 Images Guimaraes only lasted an hour before being withdrawn (Image: Getty)

‌



Paul Merson, a Sky Sports pundit who played 423 games for the Gunners between 1985 and 1997, pulled no punches with his assessment of the £75million man. He said: "A million miles off it. I said at half-time he would come off, but he's stayed on for another 10 minutes or so. It was really quick for him. They closed him down.

"I don't care how good you are. If people get your head down and close you down and make you work, it's a leveller and that's what Brighton have done. They have been absolutely brilliant."

Guimaraes partnered Rice for the entirety of the second half during Arsenal's previous Premier League clash against Sunderland. Arteta pointed to this 2-0 success when assessing why the midfield change did not work.

Article continues below

"It worked extremely well when we played Sunderland away," he said. "Today, it didn't work for a lot of things that happened as well behind them to make sure that they could play a completely different game. That's something that will surely evolve. It's in its early stages. They only play together a few minutes and that relationship will for sure improve and give us a lot of joy."

Sports.title: Real Madrid issue furious statement amid extraordinary Jose Mourinho ref rant after derby defeat
Sports.content:
Real Madrid issue furious statement amid extraordinary Jose Mourinho ref rant after derby defeat

Atletico Madrid beat Real Madrid in a feisty derby on Sunday afternoon - but Jose Mourinho was left furious by the performance of the referee

View 3 Images Jose Mourinho after Real Madrid's derby defeat

Real Madrid launched a scathing attack on the refereeing team that oversaw their 2-1 derby defeat to Atletico Madrid. Alejandro Grimaldo put the hosts ahead with a second-half penalty at the Metropolitano after defender Dean Huijsen was sent off for bringing down Giuliano Simeone.

‌



Jonathan David then doubled Atletico’s lead before Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back as Madrid dropped to fourth in the La Liga table. But just hours after the game concluded in the Spanish capital, Real released a statement that took aim at referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias and described some of the decisions given against them as "catastrophic".

‌



The statement read: “Real Madrid lost at the Metropolitano in a derby marked by the poor officiating of Ortiz Arias, who failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Bellingham's knee (despite reviewing the play on the monitor) and Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle. Both decisions shaped the match, which was decided in the second-half in favor of Atletico.

‌



“Until the 30th minute, the game had very few dangerous plays. But from that point on, controversy took over the derby. In the 35th minute, during a contested ball, Bellingham got to the ball before Cuti Romero, and the Atletico defender planted his studs into the left knee of the Madrid player. Ortiz Arias initially booked our player but was called by Trujillo Suarez to review the incident on the monitor.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“After watching the replay, he rescinded the card from Bellingham and issued a yellow card to the Atletico defender instead of sending him off. Nine minutes later, the referee made another crucial error by not penalizing Kang-In Lee for a challenge on Valverde, where he struck him with his studs on the left ankle. Ortiz Arias was close to the incident but did not show a red card (or even a yellow card) to the Atletico player, nor was he alerted by Trujillo Suarez on this occasion.

“In the 50th minute, Ortiz Arias awarded a penalty against Huijsen for a foul on Giuliano and showed the Madridista a yellow card. After being advised by Trujillo Suarez, he went to review the play on the monitor and this time decided to send off Huijsen. Grimaldo converted the penalty to make it 1-0.

“In the 59th minute, the score became 2-0 after a goal by J. David. In the 76th minute, Madrid had a chance to make it 2-1 with a one-on-one opportunity for Diomande against Oblak, who came out on top.

‌



View 3 Images Jonathan David celebrates after scoring for Atletico Madrid (Image: (Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images))

“However, our team did score in the 89th minute with a header from Rudiger following a free kick taken by Bernardo. From then until the final whistle, Mourinho's side pushed for an equalizer but were unsuccessful.”

While Jose Mourinho began his press conference with pictures of two fouls committed by Atleti players that he said should have been red cards. Mourinho opted to focus on two first-half incidents. The first was was when Cristian Romero was shown a yellow card for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee, while Lee Kang-in escaped punishment for a crunching challenge on Federico Valverde.

‌



"The story of the game is here," Mourinho said. "They're two clear red cards. With the difficulties we had afterwards, with 11 versus 10 (players), you could imagine what it would have been like (for us) for 50 minutes with 11 versus nine.

View 3 Images Jose Mourinho argues with Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias (Image: (Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

"It's the CTA (the referee's committee). It's all been very strange. It's a referee who, at 41, doesn't have international experience. I don't know why he was the referee. The poor guy came here and couldn't cope with the pressure.

Article continues below

"But for (the VAR) there's no pressure, at (RFEF HQ) Las Rozas there's no pressure. Or maybe there is and we don't know...That combination, a poor referee, who's only done small games, and a VAR with a big history. Congratulations to the CTA."

He then added: "The penalty at Real Sociedad [for Atletico] is laughable. The penalty for Barcelona is laughable, the non-sending off (for Barcelona) against Athletic Club. So many things together...I thought I'd find a different league to the one I left (in 2013), and people told me no, and they explained why. But we'll fight."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick denies Gary Neville claim in staunch defence of Man Utd stars
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick denies Gary Neville claim in staunch defence of Man Utd stars

Manchester United have endured a poor start to Michael Carrick's first full season at the helm but the Red Devils boss has come out fighting with his assessment of his side's performance

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Manchester United have endured a poor start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick insisted Manchester United can still have a “big season” after Gary Neville branded the performance “absolutely pathetic.”

Matheus Cunha’s deflected shot snatched a last-minute draw but the result drew stinging criticism from Sky pundit Neville as United go into the international break languishing in 12th place.

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, whose side gained a point to leave Tottenham rock bottom, could also find himself trouble with the FA after claiming refs “don’t like Manchester United to lose” as he was upset with some of Peter Bankes’ decisions.

‌



Neville was very critical on Sky about the way United played at the start of the second half and said: “I've watched Man United since the age of five. That's the worst 15 minutes I've seen them play. Absolutely pathetic.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But Carrick, whose side are already ten points behind leaders Manchester City, said: “There’s still a big season ahead. It’s a long season and this is part of the journey.

“I’m not playing it down - we wanted more points. I understand the frustration. But what bothers me is that we want better results.

“We want more points, we're going to have a spell where it's not quite going for you and we've had a spell of that where small things have ended up as big things.

‌



“We don't think things are perfect by any means. We need to win football matches. The supporters were top-drawer again today and we have to give them something to keep shouting about.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has given his verdict on Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

“I think we did enough to win the game. I think we could win it. I was pleased with how we responded, the boys kept their belief and kept doing the right things. I think a point is the least we should take.”

‌



Carrick was also asked about Neville's comments and if his side were 'too passive' at Craven Cottage but claimed that he did not share that verdict.

He said: "I didn't think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It's the Premier League and you will have spells where you don't have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don't think anyone gets that in this league."

He added: "I think we can take a lot from today. I think we can learn a lot as well. We can be better at certain things, that is pretty clear, but there were some god signs today."

Sports.title: Furious Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa claims referees 'don't like Man Utd to lose'
Sports.content:
Furious Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa claims referees 'don't like Man Utd to lose'

Fulham are still without their first Premier League win under new boss Alvaro Arbeloa after being pegged back late on by Manchester United at Craven Cottage on Sunday afternoon

View 2 Images Alvaro Arbeloa was far from happy after Fulham's draw with Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Alvaro Arbeloa sensationally claimed referees 'don't like' Manchester United losing after Fulham's late draw. The Londoners looked on their way to their first Premier League victory under the Spanish coach.

‌



Lisandro Martinez had put through his own net to give Fulham the lead, only for Matheus Cunha's late deflected effort to ensure a share of the points.

‌



And while Arbeloa bemoaned his side's fortune for not being able to hold out for a much-needed win, he also took aim at the referees for not awarding a foul by Harry Maguire just seconds before United's equaliser.

‌



Arbeloa said: "We were so, so close. We were a little unlucky again but we know it was going to be difficult against a big team and we have seen what the referee has been doing through the match.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don't like Manchester United to lose.

"We were so, so close to our first victory that we are a little bit upset now. I think we did a good game.

"Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

‌



"We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

View 2 Images Alvaro Arbeloa was left furious at the referee following Fulham's draw with Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

"Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland.

Article continues below

"Now we have an October that will be so important for us. We have shown the team we want to be and if we play in this way the victories will come."

Arbeloa now has a few weeks to stew on Fulham’s failure to secure victory against United, with the Premier League due to take a break due to the first international window of the season. Their next opportunity for victory is set to come in three weeks’ time as they take on newly-promoted Ipswich.

Sports.title: Premier League propose big Carabao Cup change in £1.8bn 'new deal for football'
Sports.content:
Premier League propose big Carabao Cup change in £1.8bn 'new deal for football'

The Premier League are offering the English Football League a 'new deal for football' worth £1.8billion, but they now want one massive change to the Carabao Cup

View 2 Images Premier League clubs wants changes to the Carabao Cup semi-finals (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

The Premier League reportedly want Carabao Cup semi-final ties to be decided over one match rather than two as part of a 'new deal for football'. A proposed agreement with the English Football League is said to effectively double the existing solidarity payment, which is divided among clubs across all three EFL divisions, to £1.8billion.

‌



It would be spread across 10 seasons, and both leagues are reportedly around £27million apart in negotiations. However, there is growing confidence of an agreement.

‌



Premier League clubs have unanimously approved the proposal. EFL sides doing likewise would avoid any involvement by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

‌



Andros Townsend delivers perfect response after being run over by pitch roller in freak accident READ MORE :

Richarlison takes to social media with clear message after Tottenham lose again READ MORE :

The Daily Mail reports that another condition of their additional funding would be to progress talks with the National League over new clubs earning League Two promotion every season. They cite sources that claim the Premier League wants to reduce its reliance on ownership funding for EFL clubs.

Controls on how these funds are spent are proposed, including a stop on any increases in player wages. The proposition also requires 15% of the funds to go towards infrastructure.

It also features a 'lifeboat fund' for clubs entering administration in future. They would be loaned £20million to continue paying essential creditors and operating.

‌



View 2 Images The Carabao Cup semi-finals could stopping being two-legged ties (Image: Paul Currie/Shutterstock)

The EFL want a tweak to their current divisional split of 80:12:8 between the Championship, League One and League Two. Despite the Premier League seeking no change, a change to 75:15:10 is being sought.

Under the new split, based on a mid-table finish, Championship clubs would receive £8.5million more, rising from £12.1million to £20.6million. That translates to a £1.3million uplift in League One, up from £2.5million to £3.8million, whereas League Two payments would grow by £700k, from £1.8million to £2.5million. A 2% increase in the Premier League transfer levy is to cover the increase, which would go from 4% to 6%.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The deal is around 17.5% of what all top-flight clubs earn from their collective broadcast rights. That is 6.5% more than the current level, but half of what the EFL initially sought.

EFL clubs were told about the proposal last week. They will make the final decision once it is ready for the league's board to recommend.

Article continues below

The deal has already been under discussion for six weeks now. It is said that the EFL prefers to wait until the IFR's State of the Game report, which is due to be published by them on 12 October.

Sports.title: Rosberg: Antonelli vs his mind will decide F1 title race
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 world champion Nico Rosberg believes Kimi Antonelli's biggest obstacle will be himself in this season's title race run-in.

Antonelli is on course to become F1's youngest world champion at 20 years old as he leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 81 points, Ferrari's Lewis Hamiton by 101 points and McLaren's Lando Norris by 106 points.

Just nine rounds remain this year, starting with this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix which will see the race take place on Saturday at 12pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event.

Speaking on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show, Rosberg brought up his own title-winning experience in 2016 where he faced a big mental battle which Antonelli may also need to overcome.

"I know how my head started to play games with me when I was the big favourite," said Rosberg.

To view this content you can use the button below to allow Spotify cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

"When you're really the big favourite, like he is now, it's like, 'oh my God, this is this is actually mine for the taking. I better not mess this up, I better not make these make stupid mistakes and unnecessary mistakes now because the World Championship is there for the taking'.

"As soon as those kind of thoughts come in, you start to get scared and you really start to get fear that you're going to mess something up completely unnecessarily because it remains that driving an F1 car and being at the front of the pack, of course, is one of the hardest things in the world to do.

"It is so damn difficult to not make mistakes and to be there, qualify time and time again and do good laps and not put it on the wall. It is easy to make mistakes because it's just so damn hard. Then your head starts to go, and it just takes capacity away from your concentration to drive well."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico described Mercedes driver Antonelli as a generational talent

Antonelli has shown no signs of any nerves as he has won the last two races, including an incredible drive from 19th to first at his home event at Monza, then at a new track in Madrid a week later.

In 2016, Rosberg was in a much tighter title fight against Hamilton but was in a position where he did not need to win the last four races and could afford to finish second, with one third.

He continued: "When I was going for my World Championship, the last four races, that's when it really went crazy in my head, and there was no chance in the world for me to do a pole position or to win another race in those last four races because I had like 30 per cent less capacity in my mind to actually drive well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli says the F1 Drivers' Championship is not over yet

"Usually, it's like 100 per cent to drive well, and now it was 70 per cent to drive well, and 30 per cent was just absolutely terrified to make some stupid mistake and lose my opportunity to win the Formula 1 World Championship, which is just so extremely big.

"It was a massive dream that also Kimi has been working towards since he's eight years old. So it's 12 years of dedicating his life, which is more than half of his life, towards the dream of maybe being F1 world champion. It's so big.

"That's the big one that we need to keep an eye out. It's really him against his mind now, so we see how that goes, but he's doing incredibly well."

Rosberg: Worst-case scenario if McLaren edge away

Antonelli has largely had the upper hand on team-mate Russell for much of the season, so unless that suddenly changes, his biggest competition could come from Ferrari or McLaren outdeveloping Mercedes.

Norris could have won three of the last four races, had it not been for an untimely virtual safety car last time out in Madrid, so he appears to be Antonelli's biggest threat despite being fourth in the Drivers' Championship.

McLaren have new parts for this weekend's race in Baku, before Mercedes bring a major upgrade package for next week's race in Malaysia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reacts to the news that the Monaco Grand Prix will be a Sprint race in 2027

"The worst-case scenario is if suddenly McLaren starts to edge away, and maybe there's also a Ferrari improvement or something, and Kimi starts to drop back into the pack a little bit more," said Rosberg.

"That again is similar to where I was in my championship year, because I was not driving as well, I started to drop back into the pack in those last four races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Antonelli converted 19th to first to take a sensational victory at the Italian Grand Prix

"Even in Mexico in qualifying until the last moment, I was actually only sixth in Q3 until the last moment. In each of those races, I was P3 at some point and not P2, and Max Verstappen was banging into me like every single race.

"If you were to drop back into the pack ever so slightly, again, the risk just comes up more and you start to get more and more panicked about things."

Sports.title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire to end 36-year List A trophy wait
Sports.content:
Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.

Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.

Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

Leicestershire, still reeling from the points deduction in the Rothesay County Championship that makes relegation almost certain, had hoped to ease the pain winning a second Metro Bank trophy in the space of four seasons but it was not to be.

Put in, Middlesex were 32-3 in the 11th over and five down in the 22nd - all snared by the immaculate Cox.

Image: Middlesex's players celebrate winning the Metro Bank One Day Cup

Nathan Fernandes slashed at one from Holland, who dismissed Max Holden in similar fashion, and Tom Scriven found a thin edge to remove skipper Ben Geddes for a duck.

Josh De Caires fell victim to a superb leg-side grab before Luke Hollman nicked a first-ball googly from Rehan Ahmed and Cox celebrated again.

But Duke - on loan from Yorkshire as cover for the injured Joe Cracknell - provided the support Higgins needed before a top edge to extra cover brought his undoing, Helm was leg before to Rehan and Higgins perished one ball after going to his maiden List A hundred, failing to clear long-on, looking for a 10th boundary.

Image: Middlesex wicketkeeper Harry Duke played a crucial innings

The Leicestershire innings almost exactly mirrored that of Middlesex as they slipped to 32-3 and 79-5.



Sharma dismissed Foxes captain and former Middlesex batter Stephen Eskinazi, caught at second slip, and Hamza Shaikh leg before, veteran Roland-Jones having Rishi Patel caught at deep square leg.

Roland-Jones claimed two more victims in Ahmed, leg before, and Cox, caught behind.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New England Test coach Stephen Fleming has outlined what he wants from his players going forward

Leicestershire found themselves needing someone to step up as Higgins had and Kelly answered the call. Allowing few scoring opportunities to pass him by, reaching 50 from 52 balls with six fours and a pick-up for six off Sharma as he and Holland added 50 for the sixth wicket.

Ben Green's departure added more pressure, with 57 still needed. Kelly, who twice hammered Zafar down the ground for more sixes, kept the Foxes in the hunt, reaching 100 from 103 balls.

But, after needing treatment for cramp, he pulled Helm straight to deep square. Ajaz Patel fell to a stunning catch at backward point by Zafar off Helm, before Scriven was the last man to go, caught at mid-off.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 Dream week for teenager Kostoulas

In the week that 16-year-old Max Dowman has been thrust into the spotlight, it was another teenager who gave us a glimpse of the future in Brighton’s impressive win over Arsenal. Charalampos Kostoulas – nicknamed ‘Babis’ in his homeland, in homage to former Argentina striker Gabriel Batistuta – has already started twice as many Premier League games as he did in his first season in English football, when he was a backup for Danny Welbeck. The 19-year-old repaid Fabian Hürzeler’s faith in him against the reigning champions. Despite his tender years, Kostoulas already possesses the physical attributes to mix it with the best. He caused Gabriel Magalhães and company problems all afternoon, capping it off with a brilliant goal from 25 yards, his third in eight days. “We always knew that he’s capable of scoring goals out of nowhere,” said Hürzeler. “He just has this intrinsic motivation of really improving every day. He gets more and more professional, he understands the demands from the Premier League more, he understands our demands.” Ed Aarons

View image in fullscreen Charalampos Kostoulas fires in a shot during Brighton’s impressive win against Arsenal. Photograph: Simon Dack/TPI/Shutterstock

2 Jacquet required as Liverpool tighten up

Alexander Isak may have been Liverpool’s match-winner on Andoni Iraola’s return to Bournemouth, but it was an afternoon to celebrate defence rather than attack. Liverpool’s front four, signed for a combined £400m, were shorn of fluidity and chemistry. The real stars were in defence, with Ronald Araújo strong at right-back and Jérémy Jacquet commanding at centre-back. Liverpool have kept three straight clean sheets in the league for the first time since the start of last season, and Jacquet’s partnership with Virgil van Dijk is blossoming. Last week the 21-year-old, a £60m arrival from Rennes, was named in Zinedine Zidane’s France squad in his first senior call-up. “He is adapting really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said of Jacquet. “I think in the first games, physically he was feeling the change of rhythm, he was finishing with cramps, really tired and we had to sub him. Today [Sunday] has been a step forward.” Ben Fisher

3 Worrying signs for Carrick’s sluggish side

Michael Carrick is far too phlegmatic to describe anything in such terms, but Manchester United’s game at Fulham was a must-win for the head coach – and they failed to win it. Going into the extended international break, United desperately needed a positive, but instead had to settle for a draw, clinched by Matheus Cunha. Despite the late equaliser, there were plenty of worrying signs for Carrick. One might have assumed United would come out all guns blazing at Craven Cottage in an attempt to seize control and change the narrative after a poor week, in which they had lost twice. Yet for long periods they were lethargic, lacking intensity off the ball and looking short of snap and fizz in the final third. Of particular concern to Carrick will be United’s profligacy in attack; they managed 29 shots at Fulham, but only six were on target and their goal needed a huge deflection to beat Bernd Leno. Dominic Booth

4 Trafford making strong England case

With Dean Henderson absent from the Crystal Palace net and upcoming England squad, James Trafford had a further chance to impress Thomas Tuchel. Admittedly, Trafford spent a long time being very quiet and barely had anything to do in the first half, but after the break he showed why he is so highly thought of, costing Leeds more than £40m in the summer. The former Manchester City goalkeeper made a fine save down to his right from a Yéremy Pino free-kick when the Spaniard surprised him from the edge of the box. Furthermore, Trafford’s ability with the ball at his feet makes him a true competitor for Jordan Pickford at international level. If he carries on being a calming influence at Elland Road, he could become his country’s No 1 before too long. Will Unwin

View image in fullscreen James Trafford clears just in time ahead of Newcastle’s Yoane Wissa. The Leeds keeper’s composure with the ball at his feet is impressive. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

5 Brobbey finds scoring touch at Etihad

For an initial €20m (£17.2m) outlay to Ajax last summer, Brian Brobbey appears a bargain at No 9 as the 24-year-old’s hat-trick in Sunderland’s 5-3 loss at Manchester City underlined. These were the Dutchman’s first goals – all poacher’s finishes – in the sixth game of the season but Régis Le Bris had been unconcerned. “It’s really positive for a striker [to score three] – when you don’t score it’s still possible to tell the story differently [that he is failing] but for us it is really clear that he is a good striker and he’s getting better game after game. It’s just a question of time,” said the manager, who believes his striker is improving. Brobbey was left disappointed despite his hat-trick. “It’s hard being on the losing side when you’re scoring three goals,” he said. Jamie Jackson

6 Coventry finally up and running

All three promoted clubs have victories on the board following Coventry’s gutsy win at Nottingham Forest. By far the best team in last season’s Championship, Coventry’s struggles were in danger of souring their return to the top division. Jay Dasilva’s superb goal and an organised performance offered a remarkable turnaround from last Sunday’s hammering by Brighton. They now enter the bumper international break with optimism. As Frank Lampard noted, facing Arsenal, Manchester City and Brighton in three of their first four games has not been a kind reintroduction. Their defender, Stephen Mfuni, 18, delivered an assured Premier League debut. On loan from Manchester City, Mfuni received rave reviews in a four-month spell at Watford, another youthful defender to make a strong impression, alongside Jannik Schuster at Brentford and Luka Vuskovic at Brighton. Though was it Mfuni that Caleb Yirenkyi tripped over for the VAR decision that denied Forest an equaliser? Zapruder-esque footage from Forest fans suggests it might have been. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Stephen Mfuni fouls Liam Delap during a fine showing by the teenage defender. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

7 Schuster shows Chelsea his skills

By the end, the talk had switched to Brentford’s attacking potency, both from set plays and through the quiet probing of Mikkel Damsgaard, but this was a victory rooted in their defending. Jannik Schuster arrived from Salzburg in the summer for a fee of around £16m and is already beginning to look like a typically astute Brentford signing. The 20-year-old made his league debut as a substitute for the injured Nathan Collins against Sunderland, made his first start against Bournemouth and excelled against Chelsea, making 12 clearances, winning three aerial duels and blocking three shots. Perhaps more than anything else in football, defending is about structure but, still, it was striking to compare Schuster’s performance with that of the three Chelsea central defenders, who cost a combined £127m despite Levi Colwill being a youth product. Jonathan Wilson

8 Maddison key to any Spurs revival

In attempting to get a handle on the latest Tottenham horror show, Saturday’s 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa, Roberto De Zerbi bemoaned his side’s lack of resolve in tough moments. “Leaders have to be leaders”, he said. That Spurs lack leaders is clear but the void makes itself felt not just in weak defending. A dominant first half ended goalless for Spurs because of an absence of anyone grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck. The £50m signing Mohammed Kudus came on at half-time, but only made things worse. Only when James Maddison came on and Kudus went wide did Spurs regain shape and focus. De Zerbi appears to be taking a cautious approach to reintegrating Maddison, who missed a year of football with an ACL injury, but the Spurs No 10 has the ability and the self-confidence to impose himself on Premier League matches. De Zerbi might need to hasten his reintroduction. Paul MacInnes

View image in fullscreen Tottenham need James Maddison more than ever now they are bottom of the table. Photograph: Shutterstock

9 Jaissle winning over Newcastle fans

Following an ultimately hard fought 2-1 home win against Hull, Newcastle and their new manager, Matthias Jaissle, were left with a respectable eight points from the opening five Premier League games. But what have we learned along the way? Principal conclusions include: 1) Keeping the outstanding England left back, Lewis Hall this summer was imperative; 2) There will be times when Sean Steur requires resting, and moments when he makes mistakes, but the 18-year-old midfielder is an immensely exciting talent capable of shaping games; 3) A current tally of nine injured first-team players suggests Jaissle needs to modify his training regime; 4) Newcastle’s current lack of an orthodox centre forward and a natural No 10 makes Jaissle’s preferred 4-2-3-1 system hard to pull off; his squad are arguably better suited to playing three at the back; 5) Judging by Newcastle’s refusal to surrender to a spirited Hull, Jaissle is winning hearts and minds. Louise Taylor

10 Attwell right to show Fatawu red

Aside from the latest VAR nonsense, Stuart Attwell’s biggest call at Hill Dickinson Stadium was to show Abdul Fatawu a second yellow card for simulation. Despite Gary O’Neil’s claim to the contrary, the referee deserves all credit for doing so. The Ipswich winger was enjoying a productive afternoon and Everton were seething over the decision to disallow Thierno Barry’s header when Fatawu anticipated contact from James Garner and dived. He became only the third player in the last six Premier League seasons to receive a second yellow card for simulation and hurt his competitive team as a result. O’Neil admitted Fatawu had “moved his leg towards it a bit” and that he had spoken to the 22-year-old about not giving the referee a decision to make. But the Ipswich manager’s insistence there was “no desperate need for the referee to get involved” jarred. It was cheating, plain and simple, and the game would benefit from referees punishing it more frequently. Andy Hunter

Sports.title: Carrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham draw
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick rejected the suggestion that his Manchester United players lacked physical fitness after they snatched a last-gasp 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday. The statistics showed the home side ran a collective 6.6km more than United, whose goalscorer in the 89th minute – Matheus Cunha – was critical of his team’s efforts.

United were poor after the restart at 0-0, leading up to a disastrous Lisandro Martínez own goal in the 63rd minute, with Cunha saying they had to give more. “In the beginning of the second half, Fulham put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said.

The draw was not the result Carrick or United wanted after a week during which they lost the derby against Manchester City and exited the Carabao Cup against Brighton; both matches were at Old Trafford. Carrick will take it under the circum­stances and he tried to ­highlight the positives which he said took in the never-say-die spirit of his ­players. They fought until the end and were rewarded when ­Cunha’s shot from distance took a heavy deflection off the ­Fulham defender David ­Affengruber to wrongfoot Bernd Leno.

Carrick said he did not agree with Cunha’s comment about the collective energy levels. “I don’t, ­particularly,” the manager said. “The way we finished the game … it didn’t look like that for me. I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. We kept pushing. I don’t think that’s an issue, no.

“The response [to the own goal] was really pleasing … the way we went about trying to get back into the game. [We] kept the ideas, kept the patience, kept the real purpose to it. We finished on a positive, which is a small step for us … without ­getting carried away it’s a good step. We came to take three points but at least we’ve taken something to build on ­moving forward.

“It has been pretty fine ­margins [so far this season] that have flipped it [the wrong way]. I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But I’m not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs.”

A section of the United support booed Carrick’s decision to ­withdraw Kobbie Mainoo in the 80th minute; the manager sent on Mason Mount in his place. “There’s always going to be ­certain reactions when you’re ­making changes,” Carrick said. “I ­understand. We’re chasing the game and ­everyone’s a little bit emotional. I don’t take any negatives or offence to it.”

Carrick was asked whether he felt a certain deflation among the fans, who have been expecting a big season from United. “It’s still a big season ahead,” he said. “It’s a long season and you’re going to have spells through it. That’s part of the journey.

“I’m not playing it down. We wanted more points. I’m not saying everything’s great. I understand the frustration. But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club. The players didn’t have that on the pitch today and that’s what will carry us through the season.”

The Fulham manager, Álvaro Arbeloa, was unhappy with the officials and he claimed they did not want United to lose after what had ­happened in the City game last ­Sunday when Erling Haaland’s ­winner was allowed to stand despite his teammate, Enzo Fernández, being in an offside position.

Quick Guide Neville says United 'absolutely pathetic' Show Gary Neville branded Manchester United’s early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years. Reflecting on United’s lethargic, error-strewn start to the half, the Sky co-commentator called the period “absolutely pathetic”, saying: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen. I’ve never seen such a lack of effort. What must Michael Carrick be thinking?” Guardian sport Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arbeloa highlighted what he said was a soft free-kick in Harry ­Maguire’s favour on halfway, which came 35 seconds before Cunha’s equaliser. Maguire felt the contact from the ­Fulham substitute, César Palacios.

“All the fouls for them,” Arbeloa said to Sky Sports straight after the game. “You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire … he’s a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them. And I knew. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here.”

Arbeloa rowed back on his comments in his main press conference but still said he was “not really happy”. The referee, Peter Bankes, gave Fulham the benefit of the doubt in the 86th minute when a Martínez shot hit Calvin Bassey’s hand inside the area. Bassey did put his hand up but it remained close to his body.

Sports.title: Maresca dismisses title talk as ‘too early’ after Manchester City take over at the top
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca dismissed ­Manchester City pulling ahead in the title race after Sunday’s 5-3 win over Sunderland, with the manager stating it is “too early” in the season.

The frantic victory at the Etihad Stadium gave City 15 points from their opening five league matches, three more than Arsenal after the champions lost at Brighton on Saturday. Maresca was asked about his team being top before the three-week international break.

“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. But at the same time, we know that it’s quite early. The international break is good. We can review what we have done and what we can do better, and at the same time, we can relax a little more.”

Of the victory against Sunderland, Maresca said: “I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game – I knew how good they are, off the ball, very aggressive. I knew it was a difficult game but happy because we found a way to win the game.

“We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals. So that means that we create enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

City twice took the lead in the first half after goals from Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki, yet each time Sunderland found equalisers from Brian Brobbey, before Antoine Semenyo’s 43rd-minute strike gave the home team a 3-2 half-time lead.

After the break the winger’s second made it 4-2 before Brobbey completed his hat-trick to make it 4-3 on 59 minutes. While Erling Haaland’s late strike completed the scoring Brobbey became the first player to score three and be on the losing side in the Premier League since Roque Santa Cruz in Blackburn’s 5-3 loss at Wigan in December 2007.

At 3-2 Elliot Anderson appeared to handle in his area but was not penalised and City subsequently launched the attack that created Semenyo’s second.

Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, said: “It was hard to see that as not a handball. It is what it is and we have to accept the decision. It’s hard to comment. It’s a defeat, but we are proud of the level of the squad. It is really tight at this level against one of the best teams in Europe. A half chance gets punished, and it’s probably the lesson of the day.”

Sports.title: Isak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
At the final whistle, victory secured, Andoni Iraola embraced both his current players and those he guided to new heights at Bournemouth last season. Liverpool are not yet the overwhelming, suffocating force Iraola wants them to become but they did enough to claim three points here, Alexander Isak capping a peculiar performance with a simple finish.

Cody Gakpo was again the architect, the Dutchman the supplier for all four of Isak’s goals this season. Isak’s only other shot before scoring was to balloon a first-time effort high and wide but his second-half strike was sufficient to return Liverpool to winning ways in the Premier League.

Perhaps it was inevitable that these teams would neutralise each other. On Iraola’s final day at Bournemouth’s training base he spent an hour in the company of his successor, Marco Rose, who is yet to taste victory in the Premier League. The pair stopped talking only because Tiago Pinto, Bournemouth’s sporting director, interrupted to remind them there were other things on the agenda.

“We knew what we were going to get, they knew what they were going to get and maybe you could see it,” Rose said. “It is mostly the same after our games; I sit here after a good performance, but you don’t get points for good performances. You have to force wins.”

Amine Adli, sidelined because of a calf injury, scored a 95th-minute winner in a 3-2 victory for Bournemouth in this fixture last season but there was no such chaos to this game. The only clear sight of goal arrived approaching the hour when Gakpo bypassed Adrien Truffert down the right flank and squared, the ball trickling towards Isak on the edge of the six-yard box.

A few minutes earlier Isak had sent Iraola retreating to the away dugout. “Yes, yes,” Iraola said, encouraging Isak as the Sweden striker made tracks on the wing, white shirts attacking the box, only for his wayward cross to end up with the ball flying towards the scaffolding structure in a corner of this ground, part of Bournemouth’s ongoing stadium upgrade.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola applauds the fans after victory at the Vitality Stadium. Photograph: Ian Walton/AP

In midweek, Iraola was rooting for his former club on their European bow but promised a businesslike return to Bournemouth and stepped off one of the two Liverpool team coaches with a game face. Tommy Elphick, who captained Bournemouth to the Premier League in 2015 and followed Iraola to Liverpool, embraced old colleagues pitchside before the warm-up.

“I love it because I love this club and it is growing,” Iraola said after Liverpool extended their unbeaten start to seven games in all competitions. “They will enjoy European nights here. This stadium will become a lot nicer. I was delighted to see a lot of the people I appreciate so much.”

All the niceties, Iraola said, could wait until afterwards. Pablo de la Torre, his fitness coach who was part of his Bournemouth staff, made that clear within the opening 30 seconds, wresting the ball away from Adam Smith to delay the hosts taking a quick throw‑in. Bournemouth were intent on building on their history‑making win on Thursday in the Basque Country and had the best chance of the first half, Alisson’s smart right-hand save preventing Evanilson’s front-post flick squeezing in at his near post.

Dominik Szoboszlai dropped a typically vicious free-kick wide of Djordje Petrovic’s post and Petrovic saved a deflected Bradley Barcola shot, but Liverpool spent much of the first half containing Bournemouth’s threats. Iraola conceded that his side were slow out of the blocks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We didn’t start with the intensity that is required to win here,” he said. “You never play comfortably here – Bournemouth put you under pressure and you have to adapt.”

Liverpool only teased glimpses of quality. Florian Wirtz saw a disguised pass for Isak cut out and Bournemouth flew forward, the alert and again impressive Jérémy Jacquet extinguishing the danger as Ryan Christie flung his body to connect with a low cross. Christie chopped inside Szoboszlai close to the touchline and Scott switched play with a pinged diagonal pass.

Bournemouth seemed to be growing in confidence but then Gakpo breezed past Truffert, usually such a dependable performer who last week was given a France recall. Gakpo crossed from the right and while James Hill dived in to stop the threat of Wirtz at the front post, the ball dropped to an unmarked Isak on the edge of the six‑yard box to stroke the ball in.

It was not a nerveless finale. Iraola hopped on the touchline as Scott, poised to make his England debut in this international window, lined up a 90th-minute free‑kick. After Liverpool won a free-kick deep into four minutes of stoppage time, Iraola crossed his hands and frantically pointed his players towards the scoreboard showing there were only a matter of seconds remaining. Moments later, it was a case of job done. “I think in life you always get what you deserve,” a phlegmatic Rose said. “One error is too much, that’s the point.”

Sports.title: Jonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derby
Sports.content:
On the eve of the derby, Diego Simeone described this as a special week in Madrid, a “tremendous energy about the city”, and it closed the way he wanted. He had enjoyed the Formula One, he said, and he had enjoyed seeing Shakira in concert, but he enjoyed this even more. At least he did by the time the last of many, many blows on the referee’s whistle brought it to an end, sprinting up the tunnel punching the air. Having been 2-0 up against 10 men through goals from Álex Grimaldo and Jonathan David, seemingly in control, a late header from Antonio Rüdiger awoke old ghosts and brought tension, but they did it.

José Mourinho’s first derby back at Real Madrid ended in defeat and recriminations: he turned up in the press conference with a picture of two moments in which he claimed that Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have been sent off and insisted the story was there. And yet there are other questions: over the way Dean Huijsen gave away the penalty and got the red card that tilted the game against them, and how his team played, how little they did.

It is 13 years since these two managers met in this fixture, their last time the night Atlético won the Cup at the Santiago Bernabéu. Then, Mourinho was sent off and didn’t collect his medal from the king. His return has been driven by nostalgia and it was like old times in the press room. He and Simeone are “companions of war”, he had said, and so it was.

It was not until the 39th minute that there was a shot on target when Atlético’s Jan Oblak pushed Arda Guler’s long-range effort away. Otherwise, there was little football but it had been heating up from the beginning, Guler the first to confront the referee after a foul by Álex Baena. To which he responded by fouling Baena back. From the bench, something was said and Diego Simeone was booked; the scene had been set.

Atlético probed from wide, almost always the right wing. An advance on that side led to Ibrahima Konaté doubting and Giuliano Simeone flashing wide. At the other end Vinícius Júnior shot over twice before the half’s most significant moment. Which, appropriately, was not about the play.

Jude Bellingham slid in to tackle Romero and the referee showed him a yellow. Bellingham, his teammates and the bench were incensed and the video assistant referee was engaged. The referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz, struggling to control this, went to the screen where he saw Romero’s studs hit Bellingham’s knee. The decision was reversed, the Englishman’s yellow taken away and shown to the Argentinian instead. The hosts still felt it should have been red for Bellingham. When Lee’s studs went in on Federico Valverde’s ankle, Real did too. Confrontations continued, words exchanged, but chances didn’t come. At half-time Atlético’s goalkeeper coach and Real’s assistant were sent off.

The second half began with Koke introduced and Baena forcing a save. It was Atlético’s first shot on target and the start of a different game. Their second soon after gave them the lead and an advantage that was even bigger. A long ball from David Hancko dropped into the run of Simeone and as he dashed into the area Huijsen dragged him down. Ortiz pointed to the spot. He was also called to the screen again – not to overturn the penalty but to change the colour of the card. Huijsen walked, Grimaldo scored and the Metropolitano exploded.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s Dean Huijsen fouls Giuliano Simeone leading to a penalty and a red card for the defender. Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

You suspected Mourinho would too. First, he removed Guler and Vinícius to introduce Yan Diomandé and Rüdiger. Vinícius had done little and a readjustment was required but there have been times when decisions like this – the Brazilian’s removal in last year’s clásico was the beginning of the end for Xabi Alonso – have caused splits. It did not improve things either. Instead, Real were oddly passive and Atlético doubled the lead. It came from the right where Lee, outstanding, worked the ball to Simeone. His low cross, bent behind Madrid’s back four, was perfect. Six yards out, David turned it in.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Still Atlético came. Courtois made an extraordinary save from Romero and Konaté cleared off the line from Julián Alvarez. Real could do nothing, seemingly concerned only with limiting the damage. Oblak barely saw them. Real did not touch the ball in his area until they scored. Kylian Mbappé barely touched the ball anywhere. Inside Atlético’s half, a pigeon pecked the grass, uninterrupted.

When Diomandé did at last dash into that space with 15 minutes to go, Oblak saved, the opportunity to make a match of this wasted. Or so it seemed until, from a dead ball that was too late even for them, Rüdiger headed in to spark a rebellion that would prove brief and incomplete, unlike Simeone’s week.

Sports.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
Sports.content:
If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart.

That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years.

It has become a day that is no longer relished but dreaded, a failure not just of the two fanbases themselves but the authorities who have allowed the ugliness to fester, who have talked a tough game on sectarianism but done little in practice to combat it at source.

But nothing could spoil the mood of Derek McInnes’s team, humming after a tough start to the season and now able to toast a second victory over their rivals in the space of a week. For Celtic, sitting on three straight defeats, the silence will be filled with plenty of noises and voices over the coming international break: awkward questions and painful decisions that last season’s dramatic double may have forestalled but which can no longer be avoided.

The drop in standards over the opening weeks of this season has been alarming, and at 74 years of age Martin O’Neill is wise enough and self-aware enough to know that he may be as much part of the problem as part of the solution. For him, the next few weeks will be a time of “self-reflection” on his role and his future, on whether he truly has the energy in him for one last fight.

“It’s a matter of whether I can help the team, and I’ll have a look at that this week,” he said. “Every time things don’t go so well, age plays a part, and you know what, they may be right. I’m 110 in two years’ time. That may be time to wrap it up. But I’ll see how it goes.

View image in fullscreen Tempers flare between Rangers manager Derek McInnes (right) and his opposite number, Martin O’Neill, at Celtic Park. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Let me generalise a little bit. I got an opportunity to come back last October which I never thought would happen in my life. Winning the league, the game against Hearts, was one of the great moments of my managerial time. But even then, I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy, the desire. There’s nothing great about getting old, I’ll tell you that.”

What is true of O’Neill may also be true of a few of his players. Is Callum McGregor, club legend but now 33 years of age and increasingly off the pace, still fit for purpose? Does Liam Scales need replacing? Does Kieran Tierney still have the legs? What exactly is James Forrest still doing about the place? And in the meantime, would you remotely trust the Celtic board – still essentially hollow of footballing expertise – to oversee the required transition?

Not on this evidence. The summer signings – Kasper Høgh, Mika Baur, Camilo Durán – largely disappeared from view.
