World.title: US seeks ‘AI dialogue’ with China as officials set stage for Trump-Xi summit
World.content:
New York – US and Chinese economic officials discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns at meetings Sunday as they set the stage for a summit of the countries’ top leaders this week.

“We just had a very successful engagement with the Chinese on trade and AI,” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters after long talks with a team led by Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng.

The talks are a prelude to a planned White House meeting on Thursday of the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The discussions, which also included the top US trade official Jamieson Greer, lasted around eight hours at JPMorgan Chase’s headquarters in New York.

Bessant said the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”

“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.

Such notifications are for potential “incidents,” or a situation “that rises up to a national security level from AI,” he said, adding that both sides have agreed to meet again.

Bessent and He also spoke one-on-one during the day, a source familiar with the matter said.

Chinese official Li Chenggang, who was elevated to a top-level international trade representative post shortly before the meetings, was present in the New York talks too. But the Chinese delegation did not address reporters.

Greer stressed Sunday it is “imperative that we are able to work together.”

Both sides are looking to ease tensions on trade, technology and other strategic concerns. These include the possible extension of a trade truce and guardrails for AI development.

– Non-sensitive trade –

Asked about the possibility of mutual tariff reduction on certain goods, Greer said teams “are continuing to work through this.”

The aim is to identify “non-sensitive” goods that can be considered separately from trade measures in the future, he added.

Such products could cover consumer goods from the Chinese side and energy, agriculture and other products like medical devices on the US side.

Beyond less sensitive items, US officials are also seeking to ensure the continued flow of rare earth magnets and critical minerals that are vital for US manufacturers.

Working level meetings could continue into Monday, a source familiar with discussions earlier told AFP.

Previous negotiations saw China pledge purchases of US agriculture goods too, and their fulfilment of the terms could also be an issue under scrutiny.

Another issue is US economic pressure on Iran, as Washington’s war with Tehran has entered its seventh month.

China is a top economic partner of Iran that buys much of its oil output and a key diplomatic backer.

Analysts caution that expectations for the Trump-Xi summit are low.

“One of the only things we can hope for in the short term is a truce, and that this will likely continue through the remainder of this year,” said former US deputy secretary of state Kurt Campbell.

“I think you will hear the president announce the intention to meet with Xi Jinping two more times,” added Campbell, who is now chairman of The Asia Group consultancy.

Trump and Xi are expected to meet in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Shenzhen, China. Trump is also anticipated to invite Xi to the G20 summit in December at his Doral resort in Miami.

World.title: Messi, Miami frustrated in 2-2 draw with San Diego
World.content:
Miami – Lionel Messi and Inter Miami’s hopes of overtaking Nashville at the top of Major League Soccer’s Eastern Conference suffered a blow on Sunday after the champions were held to a 2-2 draw by San Diego in Florida.

Two goals from Danish forward Anders Dreyer secured a share of the points for San Diego at Miami’s Nu Stadium –- a result which left Miami 11 points adrift of Nashville with eight regular season games remaining.

Denmark international Dreyer fired San Diego into a shock lead after 12 minutes, latching on to a superb through ball from compatriot Jeppe Tverskov before lifting a delicate chip over Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

But Miami, who dominated territory and possession for long periods thereafter, were back on level terms in the 24th minute when Messi curled in his 101st goal for Miami.

Messi’s wicked curling free-kick from the edge of the area somehow threaded its way through a crowded six-yard box and clipped the inside of the post before ending in the net.

From there Miami laid siege to the San Diego goal and it seemed only a matter of time before they took the lead.

Messi, Luis Suarez, and Rodrigo De Paul all had good chances but somehow San Diego managed to hold on.

The deadlock was broken in the 74th minute when De Paul released Suarez with a clever pass on the edge of the area and the 39-year-old Uruguayan veteran lashed home the finish for 2-1.

That looked like it would be enough as the game entered the final 10 minutes, but San Diego stunned the home crowd with a goal that echoed their first.

Tverskov once again found Dreyer with a pinpoint pass over the top and the Dane finished coolly to make it 2-2.

A frenetic finish saw San Diego almost snatch victory deep into stoppage time, but St. Clair blocked Kieran Sargeant’s late effort on the counter.

World.title: Torres on target again as PSG beat 10-man Marseille in Ligue 1
World.content:
Paris – Ferran Torres continued the impressive start to his Paris Saint-Germain career by scoring the opener as the French and European champions won 2-1 at bitter rivals Marseille in Ligue 1 on Sunday.

Spain World Cup final hero Torres came off the bench to replace Khvicha Kvaratskhelia just before the hour mark and headed in a Desire Doue cross to give PSG the lead in the 66th minute at the Velodrome.

That brought the game to life, with England midfielder Angel Gomes scoring an excellent equaliser for Marseille on 72 minutes only for PSG captain Marquinhos to win the game for the visitors three minutes later.

The Brazilian defender met a Nuno Mendes cross and had his initial effort saved by Marseille goalkeeper Jeffrey de Lange before bundling in the rebound.

United States star Timothy Weah, a former PSG player, was then sent off for a second booking as Marseille finished the game a man down.

Torres scored PSG’s winning goal in Brest last weekend and now has seven goals in six appearances in all competitions since joining the reigning European champions from Barcelona. He has only started three times.

“We knew that for us it was one of the most important matches of the season. We knew it wouldn’t be easy but we managed to get the victory,” Torres said at full-time, with PSG now up to sixth in the table, five points behind leaders Monaco after five fixtures.

“Now we can go away and play for our countries and disconnect from club football for a bit.”

Torres, whose extra-time goal gave Spain victory over Argentina in the World Cup final in the United States in July, is in the squad as La Roja play their first game since that tournament away to England in the UEFA Nations League next weekend.

Struggling Marseille have now suffered four straight Ligue 1 defeats, and five losses in a row in all competitions. They therefore find themselves in the relegation zone as club football takes a three-week break.

Monaco extended their unbeaten start to the campaign by beating Lens 2-1 on Friday, and the principality side are two points clear at the top of Ligue 1 from both Lyon and Paris FC.

Lyon hammered Rennes 4-0 on Saturday, while Paris FC won 2-1 against Strasbourg.

Lille missed the opportunity to move level on points again with Monaco as they lost 2-1 at Nice on Sunday.

Algerian international Mohamed Amoura got what proved to be the winner for Nice, with Japan’s Ayase Ueda scoring for Lille, his third goal in four games since signing from Feyenoord.

Former Aston Villa striker Cameron Archer scored in a third straight game for Auxerre as Will Still’s team defeated Brest 2-1.

World.title: Kejriwal, Sisodia, Sanjay Singh get 4 weeks to reply in Delhi HC contempt case
World.content:
The Delhi High Court will hear a criminal contempt case against AAP leaders on November 16

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Monday listed for hearing on November 16 a criminal contempt case against AAP leaders Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, Sanjay Singh and others over allegedly âvilifyingâ social media posts targeting Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma.A bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj granted Kejriwal and the other accused four weeks to file their replies.Kejriwalâs senior counsel told the court that he was yet to receive the complete material on the basis of which the contempt proceedings were initiated. The bench directed the registry to provide the material, which was stated to be incomplete.âReply, if any, to be filed in four weeks,â the bench said.The court also listed for November 16 a separate contempt petition filed by lawyer Ashok Chaitanya against Kejriwal and others, including AAP leader Gopal Rai and journalist Saurav Das. The petition alleges that they were part of an âorchestrated social media campaignâ against Justice Sharma.Justice Sharma had initiated criminal contempt proceedings on May 14 against Kejriwal, Sisodia, Singh and other AAP leaders, including Durgesh Pathak, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Vinay Mishra, over allegedly âvilifyingâ social media posts concerning her handling of the Delhi excise policy case.Contempt proceedings were also initiated against X user Devesh Vishwakarma.It was further noted the circulation of clips from court proceedings and said the proposed contemnors were attempting to create a âparallel narrativeâ. She observed that âremaining silentâ in such circumstances would not amount to judicial restraint but a âsurrender before a powerful litigantâ.The contempt proceedings stem from the excise policy case. On February 27, a trial court discharged Kejriwal, Sisodia and 21 others, holding that the prosecutionâs case could not withstand judicial scrutiny.

World.title: IIT-Bombay student suicide case: Institute apologises over earlier remarks; student affairs dean suspended
World.content:
IIT Bombay suspends Dean Suryanarayana Doolla

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: IIT Bombay on Monday suspended Dean of Student Affairs Professor Suryanarayana Doolla with immediate effect following the death by suicide of 20-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode.The suspension came amid student protests and demands for action over the circumstances surrounding Sahilâs death.âProf. Suryanarayana Doolla, Dean of Student Affairs, has been suspended with immediate effect. Any further action will be taken following an investigation,â Kedare saidDoolla had been accused by students and Sahilâs family of harassment and abetment in connection with the studentâs death. He will, however, continue to serve as a professor and head of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering.The institute also issued an apology for statements made in an earlier communication about the circumstances surrounding Sahilâs death.âWe apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil. The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities. In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process.âTwenty-year-old BTech student Sahil Wakode, a second-year student of Energy Science and Engineering at IIT Bombay, was found dead in his hostel room on Friday, hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during the instituteâs mid-semester examination. He had reportedly uploaded the exam paper to an AI platform to seek answers.The incident was the third reported case of suicide on the IIT Bombay campus this year and triggered protests by students over the circumstances surrounding Sahilâs death and the instituteâs handling of the matter.Sahilâs parents and several students alleged that he was taken out of the examination hall and threatened with suspension. IIT Bombay, however, maintained that no disciplinary action had been initiated against him and that he was counselled and assured that the incident would not affect his academic career.Among the studentsâ key demands was the suspension of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, Sahilâs teacher and the invigilator during the examination. Sahilâs family had filed an FIR against Doolla and âother institute officialsâ, accusing them of abetment and harassment over the preceding three months.The protesters also demanded an open apology for what they described as âdefamingâ Sahil and sought an open house involving all stakeholders before September 22.Their demands included an independent investigation committee comprising student representatives and external members recommended by them. They also sought the suspension of officials found guilty following the probe, fair compensation for Sahilâs family, and a code of conduct and sensitisation programmes for professors.

World.title: BJP MLAs recite full Vande Mataram in Karnataka Assembly despite 2-stanza order

Karnataka BJP MLAs recite full Vande Mataram after govt limits it to 2 stanzas

NEW DELHI: The recitation of Vande Mataram in the Karnataka Assembly ended after two stanzas, following which BJP MLAs recited the full version of the song, objecting to the decision to limit its rendition.BJP MLA SR Vishwanath criticised the Congress-led Karnataka government over the issue and alleged that the move was aimed at appeasing the partyâs central leadership."Even before independence, Congress opposed Vande Mataram and stopped singing it in their meetings. To please Sonia Gandhi, the Congress government in Karnataka, led by Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, brought it to the cabinet and said we will sing only two paragraphs, not the full song. To please the Congress high command, they have truncated Vande Mataram, which is equal to the national anthem. We strongly oppose this. Today, in Vidhana Soudha, if they truncate it, all BJP MLAs will sing the full Vande Mataram song, even if they try to stop us."The BJP MLAs subsequently recited the complete version of Vande Mataram in the Assembly.The Karnataka government had earlier directed that only the first two stanzas of the national song âVande Mataramâ be played or sung at state government programmes and official ceremonies.According to a government order dated September 8, 2026, the decision was taken in accordance with guidelines issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.The order states that, except at programmes attended by the President, Vice President, Prime Minister or Governor, only the first two stanzas of âVande Mataramâ shall be sung at state government programmes.The order was issued in the name of the Governor of Karnataka.

World.title: Congress takes 'Kya hua tera vada' dig at govt over 'skyrocketing' prices of food items
World.content:
Congress targets PM Modi, Centre over rising food prices, inflation.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led central government over "skyrocketing prices" of food and other commodities, using the popular Bollywood song "Kya hua tera vada" to question the PM's silence on inflation.Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on rising prices of food items, pulses and cooking oil, and alleged that the increase was putting pressure on household budgets."The skyrocketing prices of food items in the country have broken the back of the middle and poor classes," Ramesh said in a post in Hindi. He said rising prices were making pulses and other essential food items increasingly difficult for poorer households to afford."But the Prime Minister remains silent on inflation. The country is asking, 'Where have the 'achche din' gone, Prime Minister ji?' Are they only left in sermons?" he said."The people go hungry, the government stays silent," Ramesh said, questioning whether this was the "new India".Taking a swipe at the government, Ramesh wrote, "Kya hua tera vada? Woh kasam, woh irada?", a reference to the popular song from the 1977 Bollywood film Hum Kisise Kum Nahin.Ramesh claimed that prices of several everyday commodities had risen sharply in recent months, adding to the burden on households."In the past month, spice prices have surged by a massive 10% to 25%. Green cardamom has risen from 4000 rupees to 4400 rupees/kg, black cardamom from 2400 rupees to 2800 rupees/kg, and cumin has jumped from 360 rupees to 400 rupees/kg. Mace prices have shot up directly from 2500 rupees to 3000 rupees per kg,â Jairam said."Arhar dal has increased from 100 rupees to 130 rupees/kg, chana dal from 70 rupees to 100 rupees/kg, and urad from 120 rupees to 140 rupees/kg. Mustard oil has reached 210 rupees/litre from 190 rupees, and Safola oil has climbed to 280 rupees/litre from 240 rupees," he added.Ramesh also claimed that onion prices had risen sharply between June and September. âFrom June to September, the all-India average retail price of onions rose from 29.50 rupees/kg to 53.78 rupees/kg - a staggering 82.3% increase in just three and a half months," he said.The Congress leader called on the Modi government to take immediate measures to address what he described as "uncontrolled inflation" and provide relief to consumers.

World.title: ‘Our generation was mentally strong’: Congress leader Shama Mohamed on IIT-B suicide case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress spokesperson Shama Mohamed on Monday expressed solidarity with an

Bombay professor accused by the father of a second-year BTech student of harassing his son, saying that students in her generation were âmentally strongâ.

The student, from IIT Bombayâs Department of Energy Science and Engineering, allegedly died by suicide on Friday evening after he was found using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination.

The Mumbai Police has transferred the case to the Crime Branch after the studentâs father filed a complaint alleging that IIT Bombay professor and exam invigilator Suryanarayana Doolla had hurled casteist slurs at his son over the past three months.

An FIR has been registered against Doolla.

Reacting to the controversy, Mohamed wrote: âIn this suicide, I stand with Professor Doolla. If a student is caught cheating, it is normal to admonish him & ask him to leave the room. If the student was harassed due to his caste, he should have complained to the SC/ST department.â

She added: âWhen we were kids - we were admonished by teachers, parents for our wrongdoings but our generation was mentally strong.â





Mohamed also called for greater mental health support for students, writing: âI would request colleges to have mental health therapists for the wellbeing of the students.â

According to IIT Bombay, the student was found with a mobile phone in the examination hall and had uploaded the question paper on ChatGPT to seek answers. The institute said no disciplinary action had been initiated against him.

The IIT Bombay Faculty Forum has also expressed solidarity with Doolla, saying he was following institute-approved procedures after detecting the alleged academic malpractice.

It said the professor reported the incident to the authorities for further action.

The institute said Doolla and the Head of Department had counselled the student and assured him that the incident would not adversely affect his academic career. The student subsequently returned to his hostel room, where he was later found dead.

World.title: High number of SIR notices result of rule change after Bihar experience
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The large number of notices served to electors under the special intensive revision (SIR) largely stem from a key change made to SIR instructions by the Election Commission, based on its experience during SIR Phase I in Bihar.

During SIR in Bihar, the rules required electors to attach documents proving their eligibility to be included in the roll, over a dozen documents were listed as acceptable proof of birth, citizenship and residence, at the enumeration stage itself.

However following the uproar over the inconvenience caused to electors who may not have had these documents and thus faced exclusion, the EC revised the rules in Phase 2 covering 12 states/UTs, doing away with the requirement to submit documents with the enumeration form (EF) and instead decided to map the electors with the electoral roll from last SIR.

The mapping works with inbuilt algorithms to flag logical discrepancies between the last roll and the enumeration forms, based on which notices are automatically issued.

âThe logical discrepancy detecting software is agnostic and does not distinguish between a VIP and a common man. The fact that election commissioner. S S Sandhu also got a notice due a discrepancy, where his name was mentioned as S S Sandhu in one place and as Sukhbir Singh Sandhu in another, proves this,â an EC functionary pointed out.





âThe high number of notices seems to unique to urban centres like Delhi, where the electors may have been a little casual while filling up the EF. Also, the BLOs could have been more meticulous in checking forms at the enumeration stage, as this could have cut down the discrepancies that led to the notices,â said an EC official.

âIf anyone does not return the EF despite three visits of the booth level officer (BLO) to his address and checking by booth level agent (BLA) of political parties, he is either absent, shifted, dead or duplicate elector and his name is not there in draft roll.

â If the received EF are incomplete or gives incorrect information, notices are issued.

The official added that notices rarely lead to electorsâ exclusion and are resolved the moment the elector presents the proof correcting the discrepancy.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âNo elector is excluded without a hearing, which must be followed by a speaking order, which can, after the final roll be published, be challenged first before the district election officer and then the chief electoral officer,â said an EC official.

âBesides, the option of being added back to the electoral roll remains open in perpetuity. Anyone whose name is left out can always fill up Form 6, along with the declaration, on his mobile to get back into the electoral roll,â the official added.

World.title: SIR assault on Constitution, says Congress
World.content:
Jairam Ramesh in a statement said, âWith this SIR, the State has abdicated its responsibility

NEW DELHI: Citing data to flag issues in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Congress Sunday alleged the exercise was actually a massive "Shah instigated removal of voters" and an "assault on Constitution".Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh in a statement said, "With this SIR, the State has abdicated its responsibility and shifted the burden onto citizens to produce documents it may never have provided them. A test that the overwhelming majority of citizens cannot pass is just a machine for exclusion."Over the first two phases of SIR, names of 7.8 crore voters were deleted, he said. "The deletion rate as a proportion of the pre-SIR electoral roll is 13%," Ramesh said.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE | Himanshu Dhillon, Rudrankksh Patil lead India’s shooting medal haul with three more medals
World.content:
Suchika Tariyal signed off with a bronze medal in the women’s traditional 60kg mixed martial arts event after losing 0-2 to Singapore’s Hui Hoon Teo in the extra round of their semifinal at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, on Monday (September 21, 2026). Her bronze is India’s first medal in mixed martial arts, which made its debut at the ongoing Asian Games.

Controversially, Singapore’s Hui Hoon Teo was declared the winner based on her lower body weight after the gruelling semifinal ended in a draw.

Meanwhile, India’s shooters added three more medals winning silver in the men’s 10m air rifle team event before Himanshu Dhillon and former world champion Rudrankksh Patil secured silver and bronze, respectively, in the individual final. Dhillon scored 252.4 points to finish behind China’s Lihao Sheng (254.2), while Rudrankksh took bronze with 230.9.

The feat comes a day after the women’s 10m air rifle shooters also clinched two silver medals.

Also Read | Continental glory: On the Asian Games 2026

Early on Monday, India comfortably defeated Pakistan 3-0 in the women’s table tennis team group match. The men’s sepak takraw team staged a comeback to defeat host Japan.

World.title: YSRCP dharna meets PETs’ counter-dharna at SAAP office in Vijayawada over DSC sports quota jobs
World.content:
Leaders of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) staged a dharna in front of the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP) office on Monday (September 21, 2026), alleging irregularities in the DSC sports quota recruitments.

Party workers tried to lay siege to the SAAP office at Labbipet on M.G. Road, raising slogans and demanding that the government explain the alleged malpractices in the sports quota selections and take action. The party also demanded a CBI inquiry.

Former Ministers Vellampalli Srinivas and Jogi Ramesh, former MLA Malladi Vishnu and YSRCP leader Devineni Avinash were among those who took part in the protest.

YSRCP leaders including former Ministers Vellampalli Srinivas and Jogi Ramesh are taken into preventive custody outside the SAAP office in Vijayawada on Monday. The party alleges DSC sports quota jobs went to unqualified candidates without a test.



Video: G.N. Rao pic.twitter.com/Sxa8CMsA5d — The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) September 21, 2026

The YSRCP leaders alleged that the government had filled the vacancies without conducting a test, and that unqualified persons had been given jobs.

PETs’ counter-protest

Physical Education Teachers (PETs) selected under the quota held a counter-dharna at the SAAP office, alleging that the YSRCP leaders were making baseless allegations.

The PETs, carrying placards, said they had been selected fairly and appealed to the YSRCP leaders not to politicise the issue.

There was tension at the SAAP office when the police put up barricades and tried to stop the agitators.

Mr. Vishnu said the police were not allowing them to submit a representation on the alleged malpractices and corruption in the DSC sports quota recruitment.

Physical Education Teachers selected under the DSC sports quota sit in protest outside the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh office at Labbipet in Vijayawada on Monday, rejecting the YSRCP's allegations of irregularities in their selection.



Video: G.N. Rao pic.twitter.com/ECtHexTPqe — The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) September 21, 2026

The police said Section 30 of the Police Act was in force, and no permission had been given for rallies and dharnas. They prevented the YSRCP leaders from proceeding and took them into preventive custody.

World.title: Why has the Tamil Nadu Private Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, triggered a controversy? Explained
World.content:
The story so far: On September 8, 2026, the final day of the Budget session of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan introduced the Tamil Nadu Private Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeking to drastically change the statutory requirements for setting up private universities in the State. The Bill was eventually passed. The Communist Party of India (CPI), which is providing outside support to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led coalition government, and the Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), opposed the Bill. Now, Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has sought clarifications on the Bill’s provisions from the State government.

What are the key amendments in the Bill?

As per clause (a) of Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act, 2019, enacted by the then Edappadi Palaniswami-led government, not less than 100 acres of contiguous land is required to establish a private university in Tamil Nadu. Also, as per sub-section (1) of Section 46 of the Act, the sponsoring body should establish a permanent endowment fund of ₹50 crore for the purpose of meeting the expenditure for the administration of a private university during the process of its dissolution.

However, now citing scarcity of land in the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) area, the government, in the amended Bill, has prescribed a minimum of 12 acres of contiguous land within its limits. For other municipal corporations and municipal councils, the minimum land requirement was revised to 18 acres, while for the rest of the State, the minimum land requirement was set at 25 acres. Additionally, the government decided to reduce the permanent endowment fund to ₹25 crore.

Why has the government proposed these amendments?

The Statement of Objects and Reasons section of the Bill says the State government was following recommendations of a Task Force on Compliance Reduction and Deregulation set up by the Union government to simplify rules, cut down paperwork, and make it easier to do business across States. For education, the Task Force had listed five focus areas. It recommended amendments to relevant provisions of the Act to eliminate the minimum land requirement and remove the minimum endowment fund requirement for setting up higher educational institutions.

To which institutions does this amendment apply?

The amendments would extend to all private universities established under the Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act, 2019, and to Shiv Nadar University and Sai University, which were established in 2018 through special legislations before the parent Act came into force.

What is the rationale provided by officials of Higher Education Dept.?

While the Bill says the recommendation came from the Task Force on Compliance Reduction and Deregulation, officials of the Higher Education Department say that they have examined the land-usage patterns in existing private institutions and the availability of contiguous land parcels across the State before arriving at the figures.

While large parcels of contiguous land were only available away from cities and towns, 100 acres of contiguous land was difficult to find even in many rural areas. This meant that the institutions would be situated far away from urban centres, the unwanted impact of which was the difficulty in attracting good faculty. For students, too, the travel to college and back would be cumbersome and time-consuming.

In the course of their review, the officials reportedly discovered that the institutions having 100 acres barely used the entire acreage towards developing facilities for students. The basic requirements of academic block, administrative block, and students’ hostels can even be housed in vertical structures, which would also make it possible to have adequate space for playgrounds. Thus was born the three-graded structure of land requirement provision.

For the endowment amount, the officials said that they studied the current practices in several other States and then arrived at the figure.

What are the concerns being raised?

When the Bill was tabled in the Assembly, voices of dissent came from the CPI and the PMK. The CPI has since argued that such a move will lead to the commercialisation of education, which would go against the principle of social justice followed by successive governments in the State. The PMK was of the view that in addition to the commercialisation of education, the reduction in land requirement could well result in inadequate infrastructure in these universities. The Higher Education Minister defended the Bill, stating that it would attract world-class institutions to Tamil Nadu.

DMK members were not present in the Assembly when the Bill was passed, as they were evicted from the House earlier in the day. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI(M)) members were also not present in the House.

What has been the general reaction to the proposed amendment?

Academics fear that the amended Bill could facilitate current self-financing colleges in the State to establish private universities or affiliate their institution with private universities.

What has been the government’s response?

Higher Education Department officials put to rest such concerns, stating that attempts to “convert” existing self-financing colleges that are affiliated to State universities to private universities or their affiliates “will not be allowed”, since these new entities were Greenfield Universities and not to be confused with Brownfield Universities. It should be mentioned here that last year, the then DMK government had attempted to bring in an amendment to the Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act, 2019, seeking to introduce provisions allowing the conversion of existing self-financing or government-aided institutions to Brownfield Universities. The government had to withdraw the Bill in face of stiff resistance from Opposition parties, teachers’ associations, student bodies, and the public.

The current Bill treads a different line and allows for certain relaxations for setting up Greenfield Universities.

What does the Shiv Nadar University experience say?

The concerns are, however, not allayed just as yet. The experience with SSN College of Engineering is one reason why. The college applied for, and secured, progressive disaffiliation from Anna University in September 2025. It has stopped the intake of students through the Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA) counselling process from the academic year 2026-27 and are in the process of merging with Shiv Nadar University. Intake of students for the new entity will, now, be handled by the private university.

Before the disaffiliation, the SSN College of Engineering was mandated to collect tuition fees fixed by the Fee Fixation Committee, as per the norms of the Tamil Nadu government. As per the website of SNU, the fees for UG degrees for the new SSN School of Engineering is six times more than what was collected from students before.

This gives rise to enough discomfort among the student community. Student bodies affiliated to the Left parties have launched protests across Tamil Nadu against the Bill. They say that reducing the land requirement would accelerate privatisation of education, providing a fillip to profit-driven entities to charge higher fees. As has been experienced in the NEET coaching issue, students from well-to-do background would benefit, leaving behind poorer students and widening the socio-economic gap.

The jury is still out on this. Nonetheless, this move definitely signals the government’s intentions of allowing multidisciplinary universities to thrive in the State, while it claims that it would maintain some sort of control over them.

What does the parent Act entail?

The Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act, 2019, entails that the executive council of the private universities include the Higher Education Secretary and the Director of Collegiate Education as ex-officio members, as per Section 26 of the Act. According to Section 50, the government has the right to call for information and records from private universities if it deems that there is a violation of the Act, statutes, or ordinances. The government also hold the power to derecognise private universities.

In the past couple of decades, several standalone colleges offering multiple disciplines were elevated as “Deemed to be University” by the Union Ministry of Education on the advise of the University Grants Commission (UGC). It gave these institutions freedom to revise their curriculum, conduct examinations, award degrees, and, above all, fix their own fee structures and intake policies, removing every bit of governmental control over them. Tamil Nadu has around 30 of them functioning. There is an argument that the recent amendments to the Tamil Nadu Private Universities Act is an attempt to counter the mushrooming Deemed to be Universities in the State and to exercise an element of control over their affairs.

What next?

The State government now needs to convince the Governor that it has addressed every legal requirement before amending the 2019 Act.

World.title: Delhi High Court lists Arvind Kejriwal, others’ contempt case for November 16 hearing
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday (September 20, 2026) listed for hearing on November 16 its criminal contempt case against AAP leaders Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, Sanjay Singh and others over "vilifying" social media posts against Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma.

A bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj granted time to Mr. Kejriwal and others to file their replies in the matter.

Mr. Kejriwal's senior counsel submitted that he was yet to receive the entire material forming the basis of the contempt case.

The bench asked the registry to supply the material which was stated to be "incomplete", and said, "reply, if any, to be filed in four weeks." The court also listed on November 16 a separate contempt petition by lawyer Ashok Chaitanya against Mr. Kejriwal and others, including AAP leader Gopal Rai and journalist Saurav Das, for allegedly being part of an "orchestrated social media campaign" against Justice Sharma.

On May 19, the court had issued notice to Mr. Kejriwal and other politicians on the suo motu contempt case initiated against them by Justice Sharma and had granted them four weeks to file their response.

It had then appointed senior advocate Rajdipa Behura as amicus curiae.

Justice Sharma had on May 14 initiated criminal contempt proceedings against Mr. Kejriwal, Mr. Sisodia, Mr. Singh and other AAP leaders, including Durgesh Pathak, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Vinay Mishra, over their "vilifying" social media posts against her in relation to the excise policy case.

The judge also initiated contempt proceedings against X user Devesh Vishwakarma. Subsequently, lawyer Ashok Chaitanya also filed a contempt petition.

In the contempt order, Justice Sharma had asserted that the former Delhi Chief Minister "orchestrated a calculated campaign of vilification" against her on social media instead of pursuing his legal remedies, and clarified that the CBI's petition against the discharge of all accused persons would now be taken up by another bench.

The judge took exception to several social media posts by the proposed contemnors that attributed "political allegiance" and "affiliation" to her and allegedly targeted her by posting a misleading "edited" video of a speech she gave at an educational institution in Varanasi.

She also noted the wide circulation of clips from the court proceedings in the case, stating that the proposed contemnors were creating a "parallel narrative", and "remaining silent" was not judicial restraint but a "surrender before a powerful litigant".

On February 27, the trial court discharged Mr. Kejriwal, Mr. Sisodia and 21 others in the liquor policy case, as it ruled that the case was wholly unable to survive judicial scrutiny and stood discredited in its entirety.

After Justice Sharma dismissed their applications seeking her recusal in the CBI's petition against their discharge in the case on April 20, Mr. Kejriwal, Mr. Sisodia and Mr. Pathak had written a letter to Justice Sharma, saying they would not appear before her personally or through a lawyer and would follow "Mahatma Gandhi's path of Satyagraha".

World.title: Stalin warns of massive protest over proposed Tamil Nadu Secretariat complex at Pattinapakkam
World.content:
DMK president and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Monday (September 21, 2026) warned that his party would join hands with fishermen’s organisations and launch a massive protest if the State government remained “arrogant” and went ahead with its proposal to construct a new Secretariat at Pattinapakkam, a coastal habitat, in Chennai.

In a statement, he said the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government should pay heed to the “cry of fishermen” and withdraw the order for constructing the new Secretariat at Pattinapakkam. “Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should openly announce the government’s decision and construct houses for the fishermen in the area,” he said, after representatives of fishermen’s organisations met him and sought his support.

Mr. Stalin said the TVK government’s “unilateral decision” to construct a new Secretariat, “which would destroy the habitation and livelihood of fishermen,” was condemnable. “The DMK will stand by the fishermen until the government withdraws its order,” he said.

‘Other options available’

Mr. Stalin said there were several places where a new Secretariat could be constructed. “The Omandurar Government Estate, where a new Secretariat was constructed [during the Karunanidhi regime], is also available. If necessary, the superspeciality hospital could be shifted to another location and the premises could be used as a Secretariat. But there are reports that the government has chosen Pattinapakkam because astrologers have advised that the Chief Minister’s office should face the sea,” he said.

The former Chief Minister said destroying the livelihood of thousands of fishermen to fulfil the desire of one individual could not be accepted. “Moreover, the area chosen by the government is surrounded by several schools and is already facing severe traffic congestion. A new Secretariat there will cause hardship to people and students,” he said.

Mr. Stalin said he thought the proposal would not materialise as the two Communist parties extending outside support to the government were opposing it. “But it is shocking that the TVK government is stubborn in its stand. The government has created a situation in which the DMK will join the protest intensively,” he said.

Reacting to PWD Minister Aadhav Arjuna’s claim that the government had ordered only the preparation of a detailed project report and no final decision had been taken on the issue, Mr. Stalin said it amounted to “deceiving the people,” as the government had already issued an order for the new Secretariat.

World.title: Karnataka issues order restricting Vande Mataram to two stanzas in State functions
World.content:
The Karnataka government has issued an order stating that only the first two stanzas of the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ are to be sung at State functions. The stand is in line with that of the Congress party at the national level.

However, the entire six stanzas will be played or sung in functions involving the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, or Governor, the order further states. The order issued by the Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms (DIPR) follows a Cabinet decision.

Also Read: Vande Mataram ends after 2 stanzas in Karnataka Assembly and Council; BJP legislators recite full version

The order acknowledges that Vande Mataram played an important role in instilling nationalism, unity, and patriotism among the people of the country during the Indian national movement for freedom. It refers to the order of the Centre’s Ministry of Home Affairs’ guidelines prescribing the singing of the official version of the song as well as the procedure to be followed while singing or playing it at various government and public programmes.

However, the order says that the State Government has considered the need to maintain ‘uniformity, dignity and appropriate protocol’ with regard to the playing or singing of Vande Mataram, and as per the nature and context of various government programmes and functions of the State, the decision has been arrived at to render only two stanzas.

World.title: Vande Mataram ends after 2 stanzas in Karnataka Assembly and Council; BJP legislators recite full version
World.content:
The BJP legislators recited the full version of Vande Mataram at the beginning of the Legislative Assembly and Council proceedings on Monday (September 21, 2026), when the recording that was officially played in the House ended after two stanzas.

The Karnataka government convened a three-day special legislative session to discuss severe drought prevailing in the State as well as the implications of Dr. Kasturirangan report on Western Ghats.

The session at the Legislative Assembly started with Vande Mataram but it ended after rendering two paragraphs.

Soon after that, Speaker G.S. Patil allowed condolences to the prominent people.

Also Read: Vande Mataram and the right to dissent

Subsequently, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar started paying tribute to former MLA R B Shiriyannavar who died on August 27.

Agitated over the issue, the BJP MLAs raised slogans and started reciting the full version of Vande Mataram.

Similarly, in the Legislative Council, the BJP members continued reciting the remaining stanzas of the national song, even as Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed started reading the preamble of the Constitution, as per the practice.

The BJP members then shouted slogans against the government for not playing the Vande Mataram in full.

The Congress government in Karnataka has ordered that only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram be sung at its programmes, except those attended by the president, vice-president, prime minister or governor.

World.title: Madras High Court dismisses writ petition challenging Vilathikulam DMK MLA Markandayan’s victory
World.content:
The Madras High Court on Monday (September 21, 2026) dismissed as withdrawn a writ petition challenging the election of Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) G.V. Markandayan from Vilathikulam constituency in Thoothukudi district on the ground that he had allegedly suppressed his property details in the election affidavit.

First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan refused to grant any kind of liberty to the petitioner after observing that the 45-day period within which an election petition could be filed, challenging the victory of the returned candidate, had already expired and hence there was no remedy available under law as on date.

When the writ petitioner’s counsel continued to persist on grant of liberty to proceed in accordance with any other remedies available to him under law, the judges warned they would impose heavy costs if such liberty was sought for. “Do you want to circumvent the law by obtaining such liberty from this court?” Justice Murugan asked before permitting the petitioner P. Vimaladevi, a voter from Vilathikulam, to withdraw her case.

In her affidavit, the petitioner accused the DMK MLA of having concealed a long list of immovable properties owned by him and his wife M. Rebecca Anita and alleged those details had been intentionally suppressed especially when the returned candidate was not a newly-elected MLA but someone who had already served as a legislator who knows the process well.

The petitioner claimed the alleged non-disclosure of all assets was liable to be examined under Section 33A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 read with Rule 4A of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 and the requirement to provide full and true particulars in the Form 26 election affidavit. She cited Supreme Court’s 2013 verdict in Resurgence India’s case in support of her case.

It was also contended the alleged failure on the part of the MLA to furnish full and true particulars regarding the assets owned by him and his spouse had materially affected the right of the voters to know the relevant particulars before exercising their franchise. Therefore, the petitioner urged the court to declare the election of Mr. Markandayan from Vilathikulam as null and void.

The writ petition was filed in the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on June 17, 2026 but got numbered only on September 8, 2026. Thereafter, it was transferred to the principal seat in Chennai and listed before the first Division Bench for deciding its maintainability.

World.title: After Aleema, Imran’s sisters Uzma and Noreen also detained in Lahore under MPO for 30 days
World.content:
Former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan’s sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were detained for 30 days on Monday, ahead of the party’s September 27 protest call.

The development follows the detention of Imran’s other sister, Aleema Khan, after Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days on Sunday.

The detention has come amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

In an order dated Sept 20, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the Lahore DC Office ordered that Noreen and Uzma be detained for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, stating that the two were “prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”.

The MPO ordinance allows the authorities to order detention and restrict judicial review of such orders.

The two will remain in custody under the superintendent, Central Jail, Kot Lakhpat, it said.

The order stated that the two were involved in the May 9 protest and “motivated the workers to damage public and government property”.

“Moreover, they are again mobilising the workers through social media and public meetings to create a law and order situation, raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the government/institution in order to provoke and incite them,” the order read.

“Accordingly, multiple cases including 96/23 PS Race Course were registered,” it said, stating that Uzma and Noreen were “potential dangers to public peace and tranquillity”.

“Such activists will give rise to a situation prejudicial to public safety and maintenance of public order, if left unchecked.”

The decision was taken in a meeting held on Sunday, under the chairmanship of the Lahore DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz, where the issue was discussed and members “endorsed” the “evidence” presented by the police.

The order stated that the Lahore DC was convinced that Uzma and Noreen’s presence “at any public place will pose a grave threat to the public safety and will likely cause breach of public peace and public order”.

In a post on X in the early hours of Monday, the party’s Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram had accused Punjab police of “arresting both sisters of Imran, along with their children and the sons of Aleema Khan”.

Akram claimed that the individuals had “been placed in an armoured vehicle and are being taken to an unknown location”.

PTI lawyer Awais Younas Chaudhry had confirmed to Dawn that all three of Imran’s sisters had been arrested.

“Earlier Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were confined to their house, but on Monday morning they were taken to an unknown place,” he claimed.

PTI, in a post on X, condemned the alleged arrest, calling it a “blatant abuse of authority, a violation of fundamental rights, and an act of political victimisation”.

“Such conduct is illegal, unconstitutional, and is condemned in the strongest possible terms,” the party said.

Meanwhile, Imran’s son Kasim Khan, in a post on X, alleged that Uzma and Noreen had been “abducted”.

“This is a disgrace,” Kasim wrote, claiming that authorities had “broken into my aunties and cousins houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation”.

“No reasons for arrest have been stated. No news has been released as to where they have been taken,” he wrote.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, in a post on X, condemned the detention and stressed that the country did not “need further confrontation, rather an end to political tensions”.

Gohar noted that the arrest of “PTI’s parliamentarians and their family members will only exacerbate tensions”.

“The state must immediately alter its course of action. We are merely seeking justice and raising our voices for it,” he wrote.

Speaking to Dawn, former member of the Punjab Assembly Seemabia Tahir said, “It was unfortunate that the family members [..] were facing such brutality”.

She expressed hope that following this, “people will surely come out of their houses on Sept 27”.

Aleema’s detention

On Sunday, Aleema was detained under similar orders.

The September 20 order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, said DC Ijaz had ordered the detention or arrest of Aleema and a man named Muhammad Ameer under the Punjab MPO.

Following the arrest, Aleema’s sister Noreen addressed a press conference in Lahore, flanked by her sister’s counsel, Advocate Mudassir Umar.

Noreen claimed Aleema was “picked up” along with her driver after she left her residence on Saturday, and they later learnt that Aleema’s vehicle was parked at a police station. Meanwhile, the lawyer said they had yet to receive official confirmation of her arrest.

Police sources had confirmed to Dawn on Sunday that Aleema was taken to Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail.

Detentions ahead of Sept 27 protest

The detentions come after a string of reported actions against the PTI in Punjab ahead of its September 27 protest.

On Sunday, Sahiwal police arrested Asad Khan Baloch, former mayor of the municipal corporation and ex-ticket holder for PTI, along with the party’s city president in Sahiwal, Muhammad Shahid Chohan.

PTI also claimed that MNAs Sanaullah Mastikhel , Ahsan Jamal Khan and Mian Ghous were taken into custody, according to the party’s information secretary.

District authorities had also issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under MPO a week ago, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh.

Similar reports have come from Islamabad, where the PTI plans to march on the protest day.

However, the government has vowed to stop the march, and the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”.

World.title: Interior Minister Naqvi warns PTI against Sept 27 protest call, urges party to ‘change course'
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday warned PTI against its proposed September 27 long march, urging the party to refrain from proceeding with the protest.

He made the statement while addressing a press briefing. Naqvi’s remarks come as the party prepares for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad on Sept 27 to press for the release of its incarcerated founder, Imran Khan.

“We have clearly told them (PTI) that they can never achieve anything through such drama, and I will say again that there is still time; they should not go into this situation,” he said, advising the party to “not enter a dead-end street”.

Naqvi vowed the government will not “leave any loopholes” in its response if the party went ahead with the protest.

The interior minister held that PTI’s majority leadership was not in favour of the march. However, “if they do, then we have the Islamabad High Court (IHC) order, and the government will ensure its implementation”.

He appealed to PTI to adopt a different approach.

“Do not harm yourself and your workers,” he said.

On being asked if the government had any “long-term solution” to PTI’s frequent protest calls, the interior minister said, “I believe this time we will find a permanent solution; we will not leave it halfway”.

On Imran Khan’s medical treatment, the minister said PTI’s demand was for the former premier to undergo a medical check-up at a hospital.

He was responding to a question about whether the party’s basic demand was to shift Imran to a hospital, what the issue was and why he had not been shifted.

“There is no need for us to tell them that if this is their demand, then it may already have been fulfilled, as the check-up may have taken place at a hospital during the night,” he said.

“As for the treatment that is prescribed under the law, we will do everything according to the law. But we will not do it simply because they are demanding it,” the interior minister added.

Naqvi also spoke about the creation of new provinces, saying that the matter was progressing rapidly and that public participation in the campaign had increased.

“The new provinces issue is moving forward at a pace that we cannot even imagine. The way people are practically coming forward, whether they are chambers, traders or individuals, everyone is playing their role in one way or another. I am very hopeful that, God willing, and if the public wants it, new provinces will certainly be created,” he said.

“And as far as the movement for new provinces is concerned, I believe it is moving ahead rapidly,” he added.

On being asked whether the government was considering the imposition of the governor rule in PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), the minister said, “Look, we have already made it clear to them that whatever legal options are available, the prime minister, in consultation with our law ministry, will utilise them”.

However, he clarified that the party will not be allowed to “come to Islamabad and shut down the city for ten days. That possibility does not exist”.

World.title: Putin's party set to retain power after Russia vote hit by cyberattacks, drones
World.content:
Vladimir Putin’s ruling United Russia party won a large majority in the country’s parliamentary elections, marked by cyberattacks and a barrage of Ukrainian drone strikes, according to results published by state media early Monday.

The election, held to elect members in all seats of the lower house State Duma, is the first since Moscow launched its large-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

No party opposed to the war was allowed to run, with Russia’s Supreme Court removing the anti-war Yabloko party off the ballot weeks before the vote.

Voting also took place in Ukrainian territories occupied and annexed by Russia.

Turnout could offer a barometer of public opinion towards Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II.

According to results reported by Russian news agencies after just over 71 per cent of ballots were counted, United Russia took 57.5pc of the vote.

The Communist Party and LDPR nationalists trailed behind on 14 and 8.7pc respectively.

The ruling party is on course to retain its two-thirds majority of the 450 seats in the State Duma, allowing it to amend the constitution, according to projections by the state agency TASS.

The first official results and turnout will be expected on Monday morning.

Ukraine fired waves of drones at Moscow and the surrounding region on the final day of voting on Sunday, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze, officials said.

Russia vowed it would “intensify” its strikes on Kyiv in response, with the defence ministry accusing Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt the democratic will of Russian citizens”.

An exit poll published by a state-run pollster showed United Russia on course to win 49.4pc of the vote, close to the same amount it achieved in the previous election.

“In response to the Kyiv regime’s attacks on civilian targets within Russia, the Russian army will continue and intensify its high accuracy strikes against military targets in Kyiv,” the Russian defence ministry said.

Wave of Ukrainian drones

The Ukrainian attack was the largest on Moscow since the start of the war and involved around 1,600 drones, 450 of which were aimed directly at the capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

Images showed a gaping hole in a multi-storey apartment building on the outskirts of the capital, while another showed black smoke billowing from what appeared to be an oil refinery.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky praised the attacks, saying “our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night”.

While diplomatic efforts to end the war have not prevented mutual strikes from escalating in recent months, Zelensky spoke by phone with US President Donald Trump, who in recent days has urged Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian refineries.

The pair are expected to meet in New York in the coming days.

At least two people were killed — a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man — in two separate locations, Moscow regional Governor Andrey Vorobyov said.

A fire triggered by a drone crashing into a 21-storey building also led to 400 people being evacuated, Vorobyov added.

Ukraine has targeted Russian infrastructure with drones throughout the war, in retaliation for Russian bombardment of its own towns and cities.

Yabloko — a liberal party that had called for an end to the fighting — was barred from running its federal list by Russia’s Supreme Court, although its candidates remained on the ballot in some single-mandate constituencies.

Putin had urged Russians to take part, casting the vote as a show of support for Moscow’s troops and an “answer to those who want to weaken Russia”.

The Kremlin’s chief political opponents have been driven into exile, while Putin’s main rival, Alexei Navalny, died in an Arctic prison in 2024.

Navalny’s widow Yulia Navalnaya called on anti-war Russians to collectively cast their ballots at noon on Sunday, a tactic that drew crowds in the 2024 presidential election.

In Berlin and London, AFP reporters saw dozens of opposition supporters gathered outside Russian embassy buildings in protest at the vote.

Cyberattacks

As voting entered a final day, Russia’s electoral chief said there had been a wave of cyberattacks targeting election infrastructure.

Ella Pamfilova, chair of Russia’s Central Election Commission, did not say who was responsible.

The attacks appeared to have been carried out by “highly professional, well-coordinated groups using artificial intelligence tools,” she said.

“Over the past period, more than 1,000 waves of DDoS attacks have been recorded against infrastructure in Russia that is specifically involved in the electoral process,” Pamfilova was quoted as saying by Russian news agencies.

DDoS (distributed denial-of-service) attacks involve overwhelming a system with internet traffic so that it is unable to function normally.

She warned on Saturday that saboteurs had also severed communication lines in Russia’s far east, in an apparent attempt to frustrate the voting.

World.title: Doctor, wife and three daughters found dead in Karachi apartment
World.content:
• Foul smell emanating from family’s flat prompted neighbours to inform police

• Doctors reserve opinion on cause of death until post-mortem examination is complete

KARACHI: In a disturbing incident, a middle-aged doctor, his wife and their three underage daughters were found dead at their Ahsanabad apartment in Scheme-33 off Superhighway on Sunday, officials said.

They added that the five partially decomposed bodies were recovered from the seventh floor of the high-rise building.

The bodies were taken to the Abbasi Shaheed Hospital for a post-mortem examination.

They were identified as 45-year-old Dr Umer and his 35-year-old wife, Mehwish. However, the police named only one daughter, 13-year-old Zainab, and said that two other girls were between the ages of two and four.

Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told Dawn there were no apparent injury marks on the bodies. She said the bodies were in advanced stage of decomposition. The cause of death was reserved for the chemical analysis.

Dr Syed added that the doctors have collected samples for the DNA analysis.

SITE Superhighway Industrial Area police SHO Mohammed Nawaz told Dawn that they received information from the union of the building that a foul smell was emanating from an apartment. The police rushed to the spot and saw the door locked from the inside. They broke open the door and found the five bodies lying in a room.

The officer said that the doctor worked at a private hospital near his residence.

He was recently diagnosed with cancer, which had reportedly upset him. He said recently robbers had also looted the doctor. The police officer said the family had been living there since 2024.

East SSP Zubair Nazir Shaikh, who visited the spot, told Dawn that the bodies had been there for around three days.

He said it would be premature to say anything about the exact cause of the death at this stage. He added that they were waiting for the post-mortem reports. Besides, he said, the crime scene unit was also called in to collect evidence while CCTV footage was also being obtained.

He said investigators would take statements from the hospital management, where the doctor had worked, and neighbours to get clues about the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

He said the doctor originally hailed from Punjab. The investigators have managed to contact his brother, who lives in Lahore.

The police have also asked the doctor’s father-in-law, who also lives in Punjab, to claim the bodies.

The SSP said the neighbours had told the police about the doctor’s medical condition and his difficult financial situation.

However, further investigations are underway to verify the information, he added.

Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

World.title: Over 22,000 security personnel to be deployed in Islamabad amid protest calls
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in the light of the potential long march by the PTI and protest rallies by other opposition political parties to Islamabad.

More than 22,000 security personnel led by eight DIGs will be deployed in the federal capital and over 30,000 in the Attock district, which connects Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab.

In Attock, additional personnel to assist the local police have started arriving and reporting to the District Police Officer (DPO).

The Rawalpindi police have requested for 9,000 personnel to assist the local police to ensure security during protests, a police official told Dawn.

Containers being seized in twin cities and placed on sides of highways and open spaces

On the other hand, a large number of containers are being seized to block the entry points to prevent possible protests and rallies to reach the twin cities as 30 entry points will be blocked, including 11 in Rawalpindi.

Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), Kissan Ittehad and Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) have announced long marches and sit-in protests in Islamabad in the coming week.

Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) has called for a long march towards Islamabad against the levy on petroleum products, while PTI has announced a long march on September 27 for the release of its founder Imran Khan.

Kissan Ittehad is seeking relief for farmers and has also announced a protest march to Islamabad.

A large number of containers have already been seized in the twin cities and are being placed on the sides of highways and open spaces.

While additional police force has been called from the districts of Rawalpindi division, sources revealed that more than 22,000 forces have been called for Islamabad to deal with the marches. The personnel will be deployed under the supervision of eight DIGs, 10 SSPs and 40 SPs and 58 DSPs for whom separate accommodation arrangements have also been made.

According to sources, a total of 30,000 security personnel have been called to ensure security in Attock, the most important district connecting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab. For this purpose, additional forces from various districts of Punjab, including Sheikhupura, DG Khan, Multan, Faisalabad, along with the Punjab Constabulary, Riot Management Police and other units have been called in Attock.

All kinds of leaves of police in Rawalpindi district have already been banned till October 1.

Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, CPO Rawalpindi, issued an order to the police that all kinds of leaves, casual and earned, had been banned till October 1 except for cases of extreme emergency.

The Islamabad district administration and police have made accommodation arrangements for the out of district police officers called for law and order duty.

According to the plan, as many as 362 police officers and officials will be provided 132 rooms, allocated in 13 hotels and guest houses in the federal capital territory.

All the eight DIGs will be provided accommodation in Islamabad Hotel (Melody G-6), 10 SSPs will be accommodated in a hotel at Blue Area, while 40 superintendents of police will be accommodated in different hotels and guest houses.

Likewise, 58 DSPs and 246 inspectors will be provided accommodations in different guest houses having low rent compared to the accommodation provided to police high ups.

Moreover, arrangements for accommodation of the police and FC personnel called from other provinces to Islamabad are being made in government buildings, schools/colleges, Sports Complex, marriage halls and police stations.

Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

World.title: Bodies of 2 FC personnel who went missing in Bannu recovered
World.content:
BANNU: The bodies of two Frontier Constabulary (FC) personnel who went missing a day earlier were recovered from the Kamali graveyard in Palosi, Rescue 1122 and local sources said on Monday.

The deceased personnel were identified as Havaldar Ishaq and Sepoy Umar Hayat. Both belonged to Platoon No 59.

According to sources, the personnel were allegedly abducted by unidentified armed men from Saifan Kozi Khel in the Karam Garhi area within the jurisdiction of Cantt police station on Sunday evening.

Following the incident, security was tightened in the area, while a search operation for the unidentified assailants was launched. Further investigation was under way, sources said.

The incident comes a week after an Elite Force constable was martyred within the jurisdiction of the Bannu Cantonment Police Station.

KP witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks in August compared with July, according to monthly data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent. Deaths resulting from terrorist attacks declined from 69 in July to 44 in August, while injuries declined from 96 to 70, representing a decrease of 27pc.

World.title: Pakistan's table tennis teams face humbling opening to Asian Games
World.content:
Pakistan’s table tennis teams endured a chastening opening two days at the Asian Games, with the women’s side crashing out of the group stage without winning a single match and the men’s team also losing both of their opening ties.

The women’s team suffered a 3-0 defeat to India in their final Group F match at the Sky Hall Toyota on Monday, completing a miserable campaign that began with identical losses to Singapore and Indonesia on Sunday.

Against India, 15-year-old Aleena Khan was dispatched in just 10 minutes, losing 11-3, 11-3, 11-4 to the experienced Sutirtha Mukherjee. Kulsoom Khan, 19, then fell in straight games, 11-6, 11-7, 11-5, to Syndrela Das, before Fatima Khan suffered the same fate against Sreeja Akula, India’s highest-ranked player, going down 11-4, 11-4, 11-5 in 11 minutes.

Sunday’s defeats followed a similar pattern. Against Singapore, Aleena, Kulsoom and 55-year-old Nosheen Aslam all lost in straight games. Fatima, Kulsoom and Nosheen were then beaten in equally brutal fashion by Indonesia, leaving Pakistan without a single game won across the entire event.

The men’s team fared little better. Pakistan lost both of their Sunday ties 3-0, against Iran and Indonesia, and face India later on Monday.

Taha Bilal and Abbas Khan were unable to win a game in either match, though Mohammad Khan managed to take one game against Indonesia’s Mohammad Negara.

World.title: Trump mulls next moves on Iran amid ominous warnings
World.content:
• State Dept warns Americans to brace for ‘unforeseen escalation’ across the Middle East

• Trump abruptly leaves Camp David; tells Fox News ‘if and when I blow entire nation up is my question’; claims Houthis agreed not to fight US

• Iran threatens ‘sustained retaliation’; says Washington allies will be considered party to conflict

• PM Shehbaz to highlight mediatory role at UNGA, says envoy

WASHINGTON: The United States issued fresh security warnings for Americans in the Middle East on Sunday, cautioning that the security environment remained volatile and could face an “unforeseen escalation” as President Donald Trump considers his next steps in the war with Iran.

Trump cut short a weekend at Camp David, returning unannounced to the White House on Saturday evening as the White House offered no explanation for the abrupt change of plan, which comes just days before he is due in New York for the UN General Assembly.

The warnings, circulated through US diplomatic missions in the region, urged Americans currently in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.

Americans outside the region were advised to “seriously reconsider travel to and through the region”.

“Due to tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation,” the State Department said in its alerts.

“Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly.”

Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also cut short his US visit and returned to Israel, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the region.

Trump’s next move

Trump has indicated that he faces a major decision over whether to intensify the conflict. The US president told Fox News that he is in “deciding mode” on Iran and “big things will be happening in the not-so-distant future”.

According to network’s Trey Yingst, the president outlined the options as “wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically, or making a deal”. Trump reportedly added, “My question is, if and when do I blow the entire nation up? They [Iranians] better behave.”

When asked about meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who will be attending the UN General Assembly in New York this week, Trump said he would ‘probably be open’ to it.

In an interview with Axios earlier this week, Trump said: “I have a big decision coming up. Do I want to go in and annihilate them, or do I not? It’s a big decision. Anything could happen with me.”

On the other hand, Trump reiterated that Houthis agreed not to attack the United States, Fox News reported.

He also claimed a week ago the Houthis were holding back from attacking US forces in the region. “The Houthis called us and they don’t want to fight with us,” Trump said during a visit to Ireland on Sept 12. “They don’t want us to go after them.”

Sustained retaliation

Meanwhile, Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the US and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge.

Iran’s military central command said on state media that any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests and that Washington’s regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. It did not elaborate on the information it said it had about a coming US attack.

Mediatory role

Meanwhile, briefing journalists ahead of the 81st UN General Assembly session, Pakistan’s Ambassador to the UN Asim Iftikhar Ahmad said that Islamabad will stress its mediatory role amid the widening Middle East crisis during the high-level week of the UN General Assembly.

He said that PM Shehbaz Sharif’s address on the 25th would present Pakistan’s perspective on the evolving regional and international security environment and emphasising dialogue, diplomacy, restraint and the peaceful resolution of disputes.

Pakistan, the ambassador said, would also use the high-level week to underline its constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability and its resolve to work with UN member states to uphold the UN Charter, strengthen multilateralism, prevent conflict and advance international cooperation.

Published in Dawn, September 21st, 2026

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.
