Lee Sang-kyun, chairman of Seoul Cyber University (SCU), received Kazakhstan’s Order of Dostyk, recognizing his contributions to expanding online education and promoting friendly cooperation between Korea and Kazakhstan, reported The Korea Times on Sept. 16.

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, who visited Korea this week for the first Korea-Central Asia Summit, personally presented the order to Lee on Monday. The Order of Dostyk is one of Kazakhstan’s highest state honors, awarded to figures at home and abroad for contributions to peace, friendship, international cooperation and social harmony.

U.S. Open final: Elena Rybakina smothers Aryna Sabalenka to dethrone reigning champion

For the second time this year, Elena Rybakina is a Grand Slam champion after defeating Aryna Sabalenka. The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan toppled Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday in the U.S. Open final, denying Sabalenka’s bid to win the tournament for a third straight year, The New York Times reported on Sept. 13.

“It is Rybakina’s first U.S. Open title, and her third Grand Slam title overall. It means she leaves the tournament as both the champion and the new world No. 1: Rybakina will replace Sabalenka at the top of women’s tennis on Monday,” reads the article.

Astana Arena in the capital of Kazakhstan selected to host 2028 UEFA Super Cup

The prestigious match, UEFA Super Cup, will take place at the Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam, Netherlands, in 2027, before passing the baton to Astana Arena in Astana, Kazakhstan, in 2028. Kazakhstan has obtained the chance to host such a major match, marking a historic first for the country, Euronews reported on Sept. 15.

The decision was made and officially announced by the UEFA Executive Committee. Since 2013, the Super Cup venue has changed every year, moving to a new location each time. Kazakhstan has obtained the chance to host such a major match, marking a historic first for the country. For the uninitiated, the UEFA Super Cup is a single-match curtain-raiser where the Champions League and Europa League winners meet.

Kazakhstan is upgrading its oil export strategy: Here’s how

Astana is looking for more ways to move its oil. Russia, its principal export outlet, is rife with disruptions. Damage to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium’s (CPC) Black Sea terminal in November 2025 suppressed exports into early 2026, while the recent July attacks on tankers threatened roughly 1.5 million barrels per day, writes Joseph Shumunov for EU Reporter on Sept. 15.

The vulnerability would not be so enormous if 80% of Kazakh oil exports did not move through the CPC terminal near Novorossiysk. But is Kazakhstan merely searching for emergency alternatives amid instability? Or is this a transformation it has been preparing for? The answer is consequential: Kazakhstan is attempting a wholesale upgrade of its oil-export strategy, one befitting a rising regional power. It is moving from rational efficiency toward strategic resilience, from accepting routes toward shaping them, and from concentrated dependence toward managed interdependence.

World.title: Italy, Central Asia Launch B5+Italy Platform to Expand Regional Business Ties
World.content:
ASTANA – Government and business representatives from Central Asia and Italy convened on Sept. 16 in Astana for the launch of the B5+Italy platform aimed at turning growing political engagement into investment, industrial cooperation and stronger trade links across the region.

The forum in Astana brought together government officials and businesses from Italy, Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan, with discussions focused on connectivity, sustainable growth and new opportunities for companies operating across Central Asia.

The meeting follows the first Central Asia-Italy summit at the leaders’ level, held in Astana in May 2025, when Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and the presidents of the five Central Asian states agreed to deepen cooperation across trade, investment, transport, energy and other sectors.

The platform, proposed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, is designed to complement the political dialogue in C5+1 format by giving businesses a more direct role in shaping economic cooperation.

Italian Undersecretary of State for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Maria Tripodi said the new business format was intended to give that political dialogue an economic dimension.

“We consider that today’s meeting is important because it is the beginning of a new era. (…) We want to transform the political dialogue into investments, partnerships and new opportunities for our countries,” Tripodi told the forum participants.

“It is the companies, in fact, that are subject to transform the political relationship into a more solid one, investing time and effort,” she said.

A dynamic market

Addressing the gathering, Kazakh Minister of Trade and Integration Arman Shakkaliyev said the forum gives an opportunity to Italian companies to approach Central Asia increasingly as a regional market rather than five isolated economies.

“Today, Central Asia is a market with a rapidly growing economy,” said the minister. “For Italian businesses, today’s forum represents an opportunity to work with the entire region and to expand production and market presence across several countries simultaneously.”

He said Central Asia should increasingly be viewed as an interconnected economic space where companies can establish production in one country while reaching consumers and supply chains across several neighboring markets.

For Kazakhstan, the regional format also offers an opportunity to use existing business infrastructure with Italy more broadly. Shakkaliyev highlighted the Kazakh-Italian Trade House that opened in Almaty earlier this year, saying it could serve not only bilateral commerce but wider links between Italian companies and Central Asia.

Growing interest from businesses

The push toward a regional format is also coming from companies and business associations that have traditionally worked through bilateral Kazakhstan-Italy ties. Marco Beretta, president of the Italian-Kazakh Trade Association, said the leaders’ summit in May 2025 convinced businesses that cooperation could be expanded beyond the two countries.

“In the last three years, we have been working very hard in order to promote collaboration between Italy and Kazakhstan,” Beretta told The Astana Times. “But after the visit of our prime minister last year in May, we understood that a much wider scope of work can be executed.”

He described Central Asia as an increasingly important economic link for Europe and said the expansion toward a five-country regional format represented a significant shift. Beretta said the association now wants to expand its Kazakh-Italian business forum into a broader Central Asian platform while keeping Kazakhstan as its base.

Diversifying trade structure

The forum comes at a time as Italy expands its economic engagement with Central Asia, with Kazakhstan accounting for a large share of that relationship. Italy was Kazakhstan’s third-largest trading partner last year, with bilateral trade reaching almost $17 billion in 2025, according to Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Trade and Integration. Trade reached $9.79 billion in January-July this year, including $9 billion in Kazakh exports to Italy and $789.6 million in imports.

But Shakkaliyev said maintaining high trade volumes alone was not enough. He pointed to the big role of commodities in the current structure of bilateral commerce.

Kazakhstan is seeking to expand exports of higher-value goods and estimates that it has an additional $307.5 million in export potential on the Italian market, particularly in metallurgy, petrochemicals, food products, chemicals and machinery.

Shakkaliyev said Kazakhstan was interested in changing the structure of trade by increasing exports of processed and higher-value products. He pointed to opportunities in agriculture, chemicals, manufacturing and industrial cooperation, while Tripodi emphasized Italian expertise in engineering, machinery and advanced industrial technologies.

This ambition reflects a broader challenge for Central Asian economies of moving from exports of raw materials toward local processing, manufacturing and bigger participation in international value chains.

Connectivity as central theme

Transport and logistics featured prominently in the forum as Central Asian states seek to strengthen links between Asian and European markets. Kazakhstan, which has invested around $35 billion in this area in the past 15 years, has promoted its position along transcontinental trade routes, particularly the Middle Corridor across the Caspian Sea. The Middle Corridor, formally known as the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, links China and Central Asia with Europe through the Caspian Sea, the South Caucasus and Türkiye.

Shakkaliyev said the region’s transport infrastructure could provide Italian producers and investors with access not only to Central Asian markets but also to wider international supply chains.

Tripodi said Italy was ready to share technology and experience to support Kazakhstan’s economic diversification, pointing to logistics as one area for cooperation.

“Our connectivity depends on growth and on being connected in a safe, self-sufficient way in large international markets,” she said. “We want Italy to be at the same time the driver of this new road to Europe and also the protagonist of its realization. Our companies are ready to contribute.”

Diversifying economic ties

Beretta pointed to logistics, agriculture, technology and petrochemicals as areas where Italian companies could work across the region. He also tied diversification to the development of higher-value production in Kazakhstan rather than continued reliance on raw-material exports.

“We need to create added value,” Beretta said.

Beretta also said one project under discussion is the development of a logistics hub in Kazakhstan accompanied by local production, including sustainable aviation fuel. He said such projects could also be part of a wider push into decarbonization, renewable power generation, sustainable development and water treatment.

“Decarbonization, power generation in a green way, sustainable development and water treatment are very important for Central Asia,” he said, stressing that Italian companies could bring technologies and industrial experience in those areas.

According to Tripodi, Italian companies have built extensive presence in oil and gas, but they are also looking to expand into renewable energy, critical minerals and areas linked to energy transition.

Shakkaliyev also noted Italy’s experience with small and medium-sized industrial companies could be particularly relevant for Central Asia, where governments are seeking investment that creates production capacity and jobs.

In her remarks, Tripodi noted the region offered a large and relatively young market of around 80 million people, combined with energy resources, critical materials and a strategic position between Europe and Asia. The country sees potential for its companies in sectors where Central Asian governments are trying to move further up value chains, she said.

Tripodi said Italian companies could contribute through design, engineering and industrial technologies as Central Asian economies seek greater diversification.

World.title: Azerbaijan security service terrorism case spans five countries – what  is known so far?
World.content:
Azerbaijan security service operation in five countries

Azerbaijan says money collected for religious ceremonies was transferred to terrorist organisations using cryptocurrency. In a statement issued on 18 September, the State Security Service (SSS) said the alleged financing scheme and preparations to assassinate public and religious figures were being investigated as part of the same criminal case.

However, the statement published by the media does not specify the amount of money involved, the organisations alleged to have received it, or the five countries where the operations were carried out.

Information available from open sources does not allow the scale of the case to be independently verified. Available reports largely repeat the account provided by the agency conducting the investigation.

Charges brought

The SSS named the defendants as Vugar Abdullayev, Jalal Hajiyev, Javid Aliyev, Nijat Ahmadov, Nazim Aliyev, Ilkin Hasanzade, Aykhan Huseynov, Elshan Asgarov, Fakhraddin Imanov, Nail Rasulov and Elgun Ismayilov. Although the statement says 10 people were detained, it lists 11 defendants. The reason for the discrepancy is not explained.

They have been charged under Criminal Code articles relating to financing terrorism, forming a criminal organisation, preparing an assassination attempt against a state or public figure, and other offences. According to the SSS, a court ordered the defendants to be remanded in custody.

Link between two strands of case

In the SSS account, Jalal Hajiyev’s name appears both in connection with the alleged assassination plot and the financing scheme. The agency says Vugar Abdullayev and other defendants gathered information about the movements and security arrangements of the alleged targets. Hajiyev, meanwhile, is alleged to have used his contacts abroad to arrange money transfers to people involved in armed conflicts, as well as to terrorist organisations.

Although the two strands are being investigated as part of the same case, the SSS does not specify how they are linked financially. Were the funds allegedly transferred abroad used to finance preparations for the assassination attempts in Azerbaijan? Although some of the same individuals feature in both strands of the case, no evidence has been presented to establish a link between the movement of funds and the planning of the alleged attacks.

How was money traced?

According to the SSS, the funds were collected through fake s posted on social media, purportedly seeking donations for religious ceremonies. The agency says investigators obtained evidence showing where the money came from and how it was transferred.

To independently assess these claims, key evidence would include an archive of the s, payment details, transaction dates and information about the recipients. It is also unclear whether those who transferred the money knew its alleged true purpose or were themselves deceived – a distinction that could imply different degrees of responsibility.

The reference to cryptocurrency alone does not explain how the alleged financing scheme worked. The SSS does not say which digital assets were used, who controlled the addresses involved in the transactions, or how investigators established links between the recipients and terrorist organisations.

A 2023 report by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) describes the risks of social media fundraising and the use of virtual assets for terrorist financing. It also highlights the difficulty of proving that funds were intended for terrorist purposes and stresses the importance of protecting legitimate charitable activity.

International experience suggests that the mechanism described by the SSS is possible in principle. However, the allegations against specific individuals would need to be supported by evidence in the criminal case. So far, that evidence has not been made public.

World.title: Abkhaz punk rock: TOM SQUARE leader Salima Sagaria tells her story – VIDEO
World.content:
Punk rock in Abkhazia

This story is about a rare phenomenon: Abkhaz punk. Salima Sagaria and her band TOM SQUARE could be described as unique.

Salima began her career in pop music and turned to punk several years ago.

“People say different things to me. Many are supportive and say they are glad that this kind of music has finally appeared in Abkhazia. But there is also a lot of hate. At the beginning of the year, I posted a clip from my new song online. I wasn’t wearing any make-up, I was in ordinary clothes at home, just sitting there and shaking my hair around. For some reason, that really shocked a lot of people. I received threats and was even cursed.

“Our latest track is about exactly that: why so many people are afraid of change, and why our society does not want to move forward and change. This attachment to tradition also manifests itself in preventing creative people from expressing themselves,” Salima says.

“But I’m going to keep going, releasing new tracks and mixing different styles. I want to bring traditional instruments and choir into punk rock. I like introducing something new.”

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: Mass illness among children at Tbilisi kindergartens: norovirus explanation questioned
World.content:
Tbilisi kindergarten children hospitalised

Norovirus has been identified as the cause of the mass illness among children in Tbilisi’s public kindergartens. Georgia’s National Center for Disease Control and Public Health said on 20 September that the epidemiological investigation is still ongoing and that further information will be provided once the final results are available.

However, many specialists said that the widespread symptoms reported among dozens of children from different kindergartens raised additional questions.

On 18 September, dozens of children attending public kindergartens were hospitalized overnight with vomiting and abdominal pain. Several kindergartens were temporarily closed.

Norovirus is one of the most contagious viruses and causes acute inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract, known as gastroenteritis. The infection often begins suddenly. Its main symptoms are severe vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain and cramps. A low-grade fever, chills, headache, muscle aches and general weakness may also occur.

Symptoms usually appear 12–48 hours after infection. Most healthy people recover within a few days without specific treatment.

The National Center said that it is particularly important to replace lost fluids during this period. Anti-diarrhoeal and anti-nausea medication should only be taken as prescribed by a doctor. To reduce the spread of the virus, people should wash their hands with soap for at least 20 seconds and properly disinfect contaminated surfaces.

Commentary

Infectious disease specialist Maia Butsashvili believes that the scale of the cases could point to food poisoning.

She says norovirus is easily transmitted from person to person, including through the faecal-oral route, and can also spread via contaminated surfaces.

However, Butsashvili notes that if the cases were caused exclusively by person-to-person transmission, family members of infected children and other close contacts should already have been infected by this stage.

The specialist says it is essential to quickly establish whether there was a common source of a food product and who was involved in preparing and delivering food to the kindergartens.

She also says employees of companies and institutions supplying food to the kindergartens should be tested. Norovirus can be detected in stool for a certain period after infection, which, according to Butsashvili, can help establish the epidemiological chain.

“It is also necessary to establish whether a product that may have been contaminated is being used elsewhere, how many laboratory samples have been tested, and in how many of them the presence of norovirus was confirmed,” Butsashvili says.

Intensive care physician Ani Kavtaradze also said that the relevant authorities should explain:

How could the virus spread to 22 kindergartens at the same time, and why did more than 100 children in different parts of the capital fall ill at roughly the same time?

Kavtaradze’s main question is that children from different kindergartens clearly had no direct contact with one another. Therefore, she believes it is necessary to determine whether the outbreak could have been caused by a common food product or a problem in the supply chain.

What happened

The Tbilisi Kindergarten Management Agency confirmed on 18 September that dozens of children from public kindergartens in the capital had been taken to clinics with symptoms of intoxication. The children had elevated temperatures, and in some cases nausea and vomiting.

On the recommendation of epidemiologists, seven public kindergartens were temporarily closed.

The Investigation Service of the Ministry of Finance has also launched an investigation into the incident. Officials searched the premises of companies supplying food products to the kindergartens.

The investigation is being conducted under Article 198, Part 2 of the Criminal Code, which concerns the production and sale of products dangerous to human life and health when this poses a threat to life or health.

World.title: “Whoever stands against the people will not go unpunished” | Video podcast “Protests in Georgia”, day 661
World.content:
For more than a year and half – since November 2024 – continuous protests have been taking place in Georgia, with demonstrators demanding that the country return to the path of European integration. The results of the parliamentary elections held in autumn 2024 are still not recognised by part of Georgian society.

Every evening thousands, and often tens of thousands, gather in Tbilisi and several other cities. Over this time dozens of participants have been detained, many have faced criminal charges, and some have been sentenced to prison terms.

For the first time in the history of independent Georgia, the country has up to 150 prisoners of conscience, including women. Among them is Mzia Amaglobeli, founder of the popular outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti.

In 2025 she was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping a police officer. Protesters demand the release of all political prisoners and the repeal of all anti-democratic laws adopted over the past two years.

To suppress the protests, the ruling Georgian Dream party has increasingly tightened repression against civil society and the media. However, protests in various forms continue.

World.title: South Ossetia election: as expected, former Moscow official Marat Kambolov becomes new president
World.content:
Kambolov becomes South Ossetia president

As expected, Marat Kambolov, the prime minister and acting president of South Ossetia who previously held senior positions in the Kremlin, is winning the snap presidential election held on 18 September.

According to preliminary results, he is securing a convincing victory over his formal rivals – state security officer Murat Valiev, South Ossetian University rector’s state adviser Kazbek Kodoev, and Unity party chairman Zurab Kokoev.

After 40% of the ballots had been counted, CEC head Emilia Gagieva said Kambolov had received 88.4% of the vote. Valiev had 4.3%, Kodoev 1.1%, and Kokoev 1.0%.

Marat Kambolov is a former Moscow official who first appeared in South Ossetia in May 2026 as an adviser to then-President Alan Gagloev. He was quickly granted South Ossetian citizenship and, within a month, rose from minister to prime minister, and then became acting president after Alan Gagloev resigned.

Polling stations were also open in Russia – in North Ossetia and Moscow. According to Emilia Gagieva, turnout was high at all polling stations and no violations were recorded.

According to the CEC, the election was monitored by 66 observers from 15 countries: Russia, Abkhazia, Nicaragua, Belarus, Armenia, Venezuela, Germany, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Mexico, Serbia, Tanzania, Turkey, Uganda and South Africa.

CEC member Dina Ostaeva said that “no complaints or appeals related to violations of electoral legislation or the organisation of voting” had been received during the day.

After polling stations closed at 8pm, a celebratory concert and lottery were held in the city centre, with household appliances, smartphones, TVs, bicycles, vacuum cleaners and the grand prize – a Russian-made Niva Legend car – raffled off.

As soon as the prizes had been handed out, Marat Kambolov took the stage, thanked the people of South Ossetia for taking part in the election and said that, in terms of voter turnout, the election had broken all records.

“Preliminary data show that we have broken all records. Never before have so many people taken part. More voters participated in this election than in any previous one. Only together can we strengthen our Tskhinvali and our Ossetia,” Kambolov said.

One of the voters who cast his ballot for Marat Kambolov believes that the high turnout and the large share of votes he received were not so much the result of political strategists’ work as of people believing in Kambolov and voting “for his authority, for the authority of Russia”.

Blogger Alik Pukhaev expressed hope that the new president would “finally make South Ossetia a state for all Ossetians”.

By this, he means the possibility for all ethnic Ossetians to obtain a South Ossetian passport.

At present, the law provides for citizenship only for people born in South Ossetia and their descendants. Under previous governments, however, there were repeated scandals over the illegal issuance — and even sale — of passports to residents of Chechnya, Ingushetia and Dagestan.

Russian State Duma MP Kazbek Taisaev, who observed the election, said it had been organised “at the highest level – transparently, fairly and openly”.

He also stressed that Russia would continue to provide South Ossetia with comprehensive support.

And that is almost certainly what will happen, given that Marat Kambolov is a Russian official who was clearly sent by the Kremlin with the specific aim of taking the presidency and governing in Russia’s interests rather than those of local politicians pursuing their own agendas.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: EU does not recognise “presidential election” in Georgia’s Russian-occupied Tskhinvali region
World.content:
EU condemns Russia and South Ossetia election

The European Union does not recognise the so-called “presidential election” held on 18 September in Georgia’s Russian-occupied Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia). In a statement, the EU Delegation said the results of the election have no legal effect.

Georgia’s Foreign Ministry also condemned the so-called “presidential election”, calling it a violation of Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The EU statement says it does not recognise the constitutional and legal framework, including recent amendments, under which the election was held in the Russian-occupied region, which unilaterally declared its secession from Georgia.

“The EU strongly condemns Moscow’s actions aimed at installing a Russian official as the de facto president of South Ossetia, Georgia’s occupied breakaway region,” the statement said.

The EU also expressed concern over the signing of the so-called “Treaty on Deepening Allied Cooperation” on 9 May 2026 and criticised Russia’s attempts to strengthen its control over South Ossetia in the political, military, economic and judicial spheres.

The EU considers these steps contrary to a peaceful resolution of the conflict and paving the way for the future illegal annexation of the Russian-occupied region.

“Such actions systematically deepen divisions, threaten regional security and stability, and constitute a flagrant violation of international law,” the EU statement said.

The bloc reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution of the conflict in Georgia, including through its co-chairmanship of the Geneva International Discussions and the activities of the European Union Monitoring Mission in Georgia.

The EU called on Russia to respect Georgia’s sovereignty and cease all actions undermining its territorial integrity.

“The European Union reaffirms its unwavering support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders,” the statement said.

On 18 September, snap “presidential elections” were held in Russian-occupied “South Ossetia”. Four candidates took part.

However, calling it an “election race” would only be accurate in a very loose sense, as it was clear from the outset that the overwhelming favourite was so-called “acting president” and “prime minister” Marat Kambolov, who arrived in the region from Russia in May 2026.

Unlike Kambolov, the other three candidates were residents of South Ossetia. But that was where their advantage ended. Most experts described them as “technical candidates” — people who were not seriously trying to compete for the presidency:

Zurab Kokoev, leader of the Unity party;

Kazbek Kodoev, an independent candidate and adviser to the rector of South Ossetia University;

Murat Valiev, a candidate nominated by the Patriots of Alania party and an employee of the state security service.

None of them campaigned among the population. They presented their views on the development of so-called South Ossetia only during live televised debates.

World.title: Pashinyan’s salary to nearly double as Armenian civil servants set for pay rises from 2027
World.content:
Salary increases for public officials in Armenia

From 1 January 2027, senior Armenian officials will receive higher salaries. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, for example, will earn 2,662,000 drams ($7,353), up from the current 1.5 million ($4,143). Deputy prime ministers’ salaries will rise to 2,163,000 drams ($5,975), from 1,289,000 ($3,560).

The increases will apply not only to the executive branch, but also to the legislative and judicial branches. The state budget will allocate 25 billion drams ($69 million) for this purpose. The government has already approved the draft. Parliament must now approve it.

“How does this public official live? How does he buy a suit and a watch? We never assess the negative impact [of this factor] on the development of our state. But the effect is highly negative. If we do not solve this problem, it will lead to disasters,” Nikol Pashinyan said during a discussion of the draft.

The ruling party views the decision as a reform. The prime minister said he was confident that failing to implement the project would mean “keeping Armenia stuck in place and continuing to subordinate the logic of the state to the logic of corruption”.

However, the opposition warns that such decisions will further deepen the sense of social injustice.

“Citizens often become disillusioned and leave the country not only because of economic difficulties, but also because of a sense of injustice,” former MP Garnik Danielyan said.

Salary increases in figures

Under the proposed amendments to the law “On remuneration for persons holding public office”:

the president of Armenia will earn 2,662,000 drams ($7,353), up from the current 1,664,000 drams ($4,596);

the speaker of the National Assembly will earn 2,496,000 drams ($6,895), up from 1,497,600 drams ($4,137);

MPs will earn up to 1,497,600 drams ($4,137), up from 832,000 drams ($2,311);

the president of the Constitutional Court will earn 2,412,800 drams ($6,665), up from 1,664,000 drams ($4,596);

the prosecutor general will earn 1,830,400 drams ($5,056), up from 1,248,000 drams ($3,447);

the ombudsman will earn 1,830,400 drams ($5,056), up from 998,400 drams ($2,758).

Governors, deputy ministers and deputy speakers of parliament will also receive higher salaries.

The stated amounts include taxes and other mandatory payments.

Ruling party representative’s assessment and opposition response

Eduard Aghajanyan, an MP from the ruling party, told journalists:

“The public administration system has consistently faced difficulties attracting highly qualified specialists. The issue became particularly acute after the 2018 revolution, when the logic of working within the system changed radically. Systemic corruption was eradicated, and the motivation mechanisms were completely restructured.

At the same time, pay levels made the public administration system unattractive to highly qualified professionals.

We have been at the helm of government for eight years now. I believe that the decision to address this issue is somewhat overdue.

I welcome the government’s decision. I am confident that it will produce the desired results in attracting highly qualified professionals.”

Former MP from the opposition Armenia bloc Garnik Danielyan wrote on his Facebook page:

“According to official data for 2024, Armenia’s poverty rate stands at 21.7%. One in four children lives in poverty, while thousands of families continue to face severe social hardship. People struggle to meet their basic needs. Moreover, in the 21st century, Armenia has recorded cases of people dying from hunger.

In your 2021 election programme, you [addressing the authorities] promised to halve the poverty rate by 2026. Poverty has not declined. But you yourselves are now living better. You no longer buy vacuum cleaners or televisions on instalment plans. Instead, you are accumulating assets.

Of course, no one objects to high salaries for public officials. But given this level of poverty, should the priorities not be addressing social problems, creating new jobs and ensuring decent living conditions for people?

And this is happening while Armenia’s public debt has already exceeded $14 billion. Housing and employment remain critical issues for thousands of Karabakh Armenians. Hundreds of people still live in temporary shelters, and many are forced to buy groceries on credit.

Clearly, political calculations also lie behind this decision — namely, preserving loyalty within the state system.”

Comments from Armenian residents on social media

The decision to raise the salaries of senior public officials has sparked heated discussions on social media. Most users criticised the authorities. Here are some of their comments:

“Of course, raising the salaries of civil servants and public officials is important. But we must not forget a phenomenon that is shameful for Armenia. Librarians receive the lowest salaries [75,000 drams — $208]. Raise them!”

“After spending days and nights thinking about the people, the ‘democratic’ government decided to raise its own salaries by 60–80%. Meanwhile, citizens earning 80,000–150,000 drams ($220–414) can continue entering shops full of goods. As prices rise rapidly, they must painfully choose whether to buy food for their child or shoes for themselves.”

“They are setting their salaries higher than those of members of the British royal family. And they are paying for all this with our taxes. They will bleed us dry. This is only the beginning.”

“The [prime minister] claims that raising his salary and those of other officials is necessary to prevent a catastrophe. According to this passionate speaker, a ‘catastrophe’ is when someone asks where an official got his suit or watch. I wonder who will ask him what he plans to spend those 2,662,000 drams — around $7,400 — a month on, considering how expensive he is for the state. For nine years now, you have paid neither rent nor utility bills, car expenses, petrol or maintenance costs.”

Salary increases for public officials in Armenia

World.title: Tbilisi condemns “presidential election” in Georgia’s Russian-occupied Tskhinvali region
World.content:
Georgia condemns Russia over South Ossetia election

Georgia’s Foreign Ministry condemned the so-called “presidential election” held on 18 September in the Russian-occupied Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia), calling it a violation of Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

According to the ministry’s statement, “the opening of polling stations by Russia in the occupied territory without the consent of the Georgian government is a gross violation of Georgia’s sovereignty and another manifestation of Russia’s policy aimed at the de facto annexation of Georgia’s regions.”

Georgia’s Foreign Ministry said that holding the so-called election violates fundamental norms and principles of international law and cannot legitimise the occupation regime in Tskhinvali or change the region’s status under international law as part of Georgia.

“Holding any so-called elections in Georgia’s occupied territories, which are under military occupation and the effective control of the Russian Federation, while internally displaced persons and refugees are not given the opportunity to return to their homes safely and with dignity, is illegal and cannot have any international legal consequences,” the ministry said.

Tbilisi also condemned Russia’s decision to open polling stations for the Russian State Duma election in occupied Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region from 18 to 20 September.

The Foreign Ministry called on the international community to properly assess and condemn Russia’s actions and ensure an appropriate international legal and political response.

“Georgia continues to call on the international community to firmly protect Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders and support a peaceful resolution of the conflict,” the statement said.

World.title: Uzbekistan taps South Korean expertise for AI Data Hub
World.content:
Photo: The Ministry of Investment, Industry, and Trade of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 21. Uzbekistan and South Korea are exploring cooperation on artificial intelligence data infrastructure and the development of datasets for training AI models, following a Sept. 18 meeting on Tashkent’s planned AI Data Hub.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Digital Technologies of Uzbekistan, following a meeting between Uzbekistan’s Deputy Minister of Digital Technologies Jamol Makhsudov, IT Park Uzbekistan Executive Director Jahongir Rajabov and representatives of South Korea’s National Information Society Agency (NIA).

The sides discussed prospects for cooperation in e-government, data infrastructure and the digital transformation of public services in Uzbekistan.

Particular attention was given to the planned AI Data Hub, a data platform designed to support the development of AI-based solutions. The discussions focused on creating and preparing datasets that can be used to train artificial intelligence models.

Following the talks, the sides agreed to continue exploring areas of cooperation under the AI Data Hub project. This could include sharing NIA’s experience in developing data platforms, preparing datasets and building the infrastructure required to support AI applications.

The parties also plan to examine the format and scope of NIA’s expert support during implementation of the project in Uzbekistan.

“Uzbekistan and NIA agreed to continue exploring cooperation under the AI Data Hub project, including the exchange of experience in platform development, dataset preparation and infrastructure creation,” the Uzbek side said.

Established in 1987, NIA is a South Korean state agency specializing in digital transformation and information and communication technologies. Its areas of work include artificial intelligence, digital government, data infrastructure, ICT and digital education. In 2025, NIA provided around 1.18 billion units of public data through its AI Hub platform for the development and training of AI models.

The cooperation discussions are part of Uzbekistan’s broader efforts to develop digital infrastructure and expand the use of artificial intelligence in public services and the wider economy.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Syria turn new economic framework into projects
World.content:
Photo: The Ministry of Investment, Industry, and Trade of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 21. Uzbekistan and Syria are working to translate a new institutional framework for economic cooperation into trade contracts, investment projects and direct business ties following a business forum held in Tashkent on Sept. 19.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade of Uzbekistan, following the forum attended by Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Laziz Kudratov, Syrian Minister of Economy and Industry Muhammad Nidal al-Shaar, and representatives of trade and industry associations from both countries.

The Syrian delegation included executives from companies operating in textiles, pharmaceuticals, food processing, chemicals, agriculture, construction materials and electrical engineering, providing a broad base for discussions on potential trade and investment projects.

The forum followed intergovernmental talks held the previous day, when Uzbekistan and Syria signed a memorandum establishing a Joint Economic and Trade Committee and agreed to develop a Business Council. The new mechanisms are intended to provide a regular framework for government and business engagement.

The sides also discussed new platforms to promote bilateral trade. A “Made in Uzbekistan” exhibition is planned in Aleppo and Damascus in February 2027, while an exhibition of Syrian products is expected to be held in Tashkent later in 2027.

Uzbekistan’s existing Trading House in Aleppo is expected to serve as a permanent platform for promoting Uzbek products, identifying potential partners and developing new commercial initiatives.

The two countries also outlined measures to support companies entering each other’s markets. Uzbekistan plans to provide support to domestic businesses through subsidies for warehouse rental, certification and transportation costs, while Syrian companies interested in the Uzbek market will receive assistance in identifying local partners, arranging negotiations and implementing projects.

“The main task now is to translate the agreements reached by businesses into concrete contracts, deliveries and investment decisions, while steadily expanding the scope of cooperation,” the Uzbek side said.

A working group led by deputy ministers from both countries has been established to advance sector-specific cooperation. Its work will focus on identifying specific projects, companies and practical solutions, with key initiatives expected to be consolidated into a single roadmap.

The business forum concluded with B2B and B2G meetings, where companies discussed specific products and projects, identified potential partners and agreed on next steps for developing bilateral trade and investment cooperation.

Deputy Chief of the Main Department of Internal Security and Investigations – Chief of the Military Police Department, Major General Elgun Aliyev briefed the Minister of Defense, Colonel General Zakir Hasanov on the activities of the Military Police, FOB, and the organization of troop service.

It was noted that the activities conducted at the OCC base have been aligned with relevant NATO standards and are aimed at ensuring interoperability in peacekeeping operations.

The leadership inspected facilities and conditions established within the unit’s area and reviewed the barracks, sports and firing ranges, training centres for engineering, reconnaissance and driver training, as well as the military equipment.

Minister of Defense, Colonel General Zakir Hasanov issued relevant directives to the responsible officials aimed at further enhancing the combat readiness of military personnel, as well as improving their logistical support and social and living conditions.

In conclusion, a group of distinguished military personnel were awarded, and commemorative trees were planted within the base’s grounds.

World.title: Leadership quality determines companies' competitiveness - PASHA Holding CEO
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 21. Developing leadership qualities is important for increasing the competitiveness of companies, government institutions and the country as a whole, PASHA Holding CEO Jalal Gasimov said at the opening of the AZEMBA program of the IE Center for Leadership and Innovation at ADA University, Trend's correspondent reports from the event.

He said the agreement signed with IE University is an important stage of the project being implemented with the support of the Ministry of Economy and the Ministry of Science and Education. “Just a few months later, we are already welcoming the first cohort of students. I think the fact that this program has been implemented so quickly is a testament to the commitment and enthusiasm of all parties involved,” Gasimov said.

According to him, the significance of the program goes beyond creating a new academic program. “In business and public policy, we often talk about infrastructure, technology and capital. Each of these is undoubtedly important. But none of them can create value on its own. Value is created by people – people who make the right business decisions, lead teams and build companies and institutions that implement those decisions,” he said.

Gasimov emphasized the importance of executive education, particularly Executive Education programs. “This is precisely why executive education is particularly important. Especially at a time when Azerbaijan is entering a new stage of development. The quality of our leaders determines the competitiveness of our companies and institutions and, ultimately, our country,” the PASHA Holding CEO said.

He noted that developing leadership qualities has long been one of PASHA Holding's key priorities. “We want to develop strong leaders in Azerbaijan, for Azerbaijan and for all the countries where we operate,” Gasimov stressed.

According to him, combining theoretical knowledge with practical experience is essential for leadership. “We know from our experience that leadership is not developed through training alone. Leadership develops when knowledge is combined with experience, assumptions are questioned, and people learn to make the right decisions in difficult situations where the answers are not clear. This program creates exactly such an environment,” he said.

Gasimov added that the program combines IE University's academic standards and international experience with Azerbaijan's realities, practical experience and the goals of the business community.

He noted the particular significance of establishing the program in the year of PASHA Holding's 20th anniversary. “We can look back with pride at the businesses we have built, the investments we have made and the people whose growth we have supported over the years. But our next 20 years will depend on how we continue to learn as an organization and on the quality of the leaders we develop,” Gasimov said.

According to him, one of the main objectives of the Executive MBA program should be to strengthen links between international experience and the business experience of Azerbaijan and the region.

“I hope this special edition of the Executive MBA program will become a genuine, two-way bridge. While bringing knowledge and international experience from Madrid and the classrooms to Baku, the program should also enable the experience and ideas of Azerbaijan and our region to become part of broader international discussions,” he stressed.

Gasimov said it is important for Azerbaijan to contribute to the global knowledge base rather than being only a recipient of knowledge. “We should not see ourselves only as recipients of global knowledge; the time has come for us to contribute to this global knowledge base as well,” he said.

He noted that the interest in the program demonstrates strong demand in this area. “We received more than 850 applications. Today, 40 people who are joining the first cohort are here: 16 from PASHA Holding and its subsidiary companies, 16 from government institutions and related businesses, and eight from Azerbaijan's broader business community,” Gasimov said.

According to him, the participants' representation of different organizations will allow different views and experiences to be discussed as part of the program. “Together with colleagues from other companies, you will be able to compare how different organizations approach problems, how they make business decisions, how they deal with challenges and overcome them, and even how they sometimes fail,” he said.

Gasimov noted that the main value of the program will come from participants openly sharing their experiences and comparing different approaches. “The main value will come from openly discussing what works, what does not work and the practices each organization is accustomed to. As members of the first cohort, you have a great responsibility, because you will set the standards for this program and shape its culture for those who come after you,” the PASHA Holding CEO stressed.

At the end of his speech, he advised program participants to consider the role of capital and leadership in the development of companies. “You know that when companies are established, shareholders invest capital, and this capital forms the company's initial assets. If a company uses these assets properly, it grows. But at a certain stage, the next level of development requires new capital, new investments, new people or even new leadership,” Gasimov said.

According to him, new capital and leadership not only expand financial capabilities but also bring new perspectives to companies' development. “But that capital or leadership does not only bring financial expansion; they offer different perspectives, challenge old assumptions and open up new opportunities that the company could not reach on its own,” he added.

The AZEMBA program of the IE Center for Leadership and Innovation was launched with the support of the Ministries of Economy and Science and Education and in partnership with PASHA Holding, SOCAR and Spain's IE University. Under the program, participants will receive education based on international experience in areas including digital transformation, artificial intelligence, sustainable development, innovation, leadership and modern management.

World.title: Serbian entrepreneurs conclude deal for licorice root extract on Turkmen exchange

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 21. In the September 15 trading session on SCRMET, a foreign deal was concluded in the agricultural sector.

This was reflected in a press release published by the State Commodity and Raw Materials Exchange of Turkmenistan (SCRMET).

According to the report, entrepreneurs from Serbia concluded a deal with local entrepreneurs for the purchase of thick licorice root extract.

SCRMET reported that one transaction was finalized during the session, amounting to $236,250.

World.title: Inside the crackdown on a $23 billion black market
World.content:
He looks like an ordinary angler, but this 43-year-old man is anything but.

In the waters between Brisbane and Russell Island, he was caught poaching mud crabs and selling them in south-east Queensland.

"Mud crabs can retail anywhere up to $64 a kilo for high-quality, top-grade mud crabs," said Graeme Bolton, director-general of Queensland's Department of Primary Industries.

" So they're high value, they're easy to transport, and readily sold on the black market. "

Last year, other seafood species such as threadfin salmon, molluscs and mulloway were uncovered at the man's house following a raid by fisheries officers.

Loading...

He was convicted, fined $10,000 and had his boat destroyed.

In 2024, a 46-year-old Gold Coast man was caught hiding crabs in his boat.

After searching his property, officers found more boxes of crabs.

His boat was also crushed.

Loading...

"This is really to send a very clear message that unlawful activity in Queensland will not go unpunished," Mr Bolton told 7.30.

Illegal fishing is a widespread environmental and transnational crime. It includes fishing in protected marine reserves, ignoring catch quotas, using prohibited gear, and international smuggling.

Loading...

These organised activities threaten marine ecosystems and are estimated to cost legal fisheries up to $23 billion annually globally.

Illegal fishing can also be linked to a variety of other crimes including labour exploitation, human rights abuses and trafficking of illicit goods.

The domestic illicit seafood trade in Australia involves both recreational and commercial anglers poaching fish and other seafood to sell on the black market.

It is then funnelled directly into restaurants, markets, and on the street.

Illegally caught seafood is funnelled directly into restaurants, markets, and on the street. (ABC News: Kathleen O'Connor)

"People try to hide fish and crabs underneath floorboards or ... within the boat or cars, [sometimes even] dropping fish and crabs in the bush somewhere," Mr Bolton said.

"Black market activity in particular, erodes that ability for the average Queenslander to go out, catch a fish, and more importantly, for our Queensland commercial fishers to go out and make a living."

The prevalence of illegal fishing

Illegal fishing has been an ongoing problem globally, but in Australia, compliance numbers are down, and prosecutions are up.

According to the Australian Fisheries Management Authority, 273 people were prosecuted for illegal fishing in WA in 2025, more than triple the number from 2024.

Due to a jump in illegal activity, fisheries officers have increased their patrols, and in the Northern Territory, 237 foreign fishers were prosecuted in the Darwin Local Court between 2024 and 2025, a sharp increase from 75 prosecutions between 2023 and 2024.

An Indonesian fishing crew were found in mangroves in the Northern Territory in 2024. (Supplied: Northern Land Council)

In Queensland, 1,809 reports of illegal fishing were investigated between 2024 and 2025, and 14 matters were prosecuted in the Magistrates Court.

In Victoria, 473 fines were issued between 2025 and 2026. The year before was more than double. 1,219 fines were handed out following cuts to enforcement numbers in the financial year.

In 2023, the New South Wales Government recorded 2,900 illegal fishing reports handled by the fisheries department. This year, fisheries recorded 3,767 offences by recreational anglers.

In Tasmania and South Australia numbers have remained quite consistent.

NSW seafood raids

7.30 was given exclusive access to a NSW Fisheries operation after officers received intelligence that suspected illegal seafood was being sold in Cabramatta in Sydney's south-west.

Officers measured fish to check if they were undersized and requested receipts for all products, which were provided.

An officer from Fisheries NSW measures fish to check if they are undersized. (ABC News: Kathleen O'Connor)

One shop that sold household goods also had fridges full of abalone — the highly sought-after and expensive product is a popular black-market item.

"We had 14 packages of abalone that weren't labelled correctly. Under the regulations, there's specifications on what needs to be on the label," said Fisheries officer Dan McGarrity.

The shop owner produced receipts to prove that the product was purchased legally, but authorities are continuing to investigate.

The seized abalone is worth around $4,000. If officers can prove the abalone was caught and sold illegally, the owner could face prison time.

The seized abalone is worth around $4,000. (ABC News: Kathleen O'Connor)

"We want people to know that they can't get away with this behaviour in NSW," state Minister for Agriculture Tara Moriarty said.

"We're serious about increasing the fines ... and making sure that fisheries officers have more powers.

Last week, NSW introduced new legislation which includes increased fines of up to $44,000 for people caught engaging in the illicit seafood trade.

Authorities are also investing in new technology to track offenders, including investing in night vision technology.

NSW Fisheries officers were acting on intelligence that suspected illegal seafood was being sold in south-west Sydney. (ABC News: Kathleen O'Connor)

'Big money' equals big risks

In 2023, a WA study found around 11.8 per cent of seafood products in Australia were labelled incorrectly.

Peter Jenkins is a wholesaler from Victoria and says he has lost count of the number of times he has been offered illegal seafood.

He says it's often whiting and snapper, because they're popular fish and fetch strong market prices.

"The population's getting greater and the fishermen are getting less, and of course everything's worth fairly big money now," Mr Jenkins said.

Safe seafood consumer advocate Roy Palmer says incorrect labelling could mean the fish has been illegally caught and may pose serious health risks.

NSW is investing in technology to track offenders. (ABC News: Kathleen O'Connor)

"That's why we license fishermen," Mr Palmer said.

"We license fishermen because they have to understand how the system works and that they must follow protocols to get the product through to the consumer."

CEO of the Victorian Fisheries Authority Travis Dowling says he has seen people try and sell fish that could result in health risks.

"We've had people in summer illegally take abalone, selling it off the street on 40 degree days in plastic shopping bags," he said.

" You wouldn't want to eat that food. "
